lenses.lens: Distilling explicit CoT into latent/continuous tokens (CODI / SIM-CoT / CoLaR lineage): what supervises each latent token, and which recipe fixes a channel whose latent is probe-decodable (0.30) but generatively unusable (0.00)

papers.title: CODI: Compressing Chain-of-Thought into Continuous Space via Self-Distillation
papers.scale_tested: GPT-2 124M and LLaMA-3.2-1B-Instruct; GSM8k-Aug 385k rows (also GSM8k-Aug-NL 385k, CommonsenseQA-CoT 8.1k); LoRA r=128 alpha=32, bf16, effective batch 128; GPT-2: lr 3e-3, 40 epochs, ~36h on 1x A100-80GB; LLaMA-1B: lr 8e-4, 10 epochs, ~48h A100
papers.core_mechanism: Single-stage self-distillation, no curriculum. Same LoRA-adapted model runs a teacher task (CE on Q+gold-CoT+A, with the FINAL CoT step excluded to block a copy shortcut) and a student task (learnable <bot>, 6 autoregressive continuous thoughts each passed through a 2-layer MLP+LayerNorm projection, <eot>, CE on answer). L_KD = smooth-L1 between teacher and student hidden states AT THE TOKEN IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING THE ANSWER (the ':' of 'The answer is:'), across ALL layers, each layer normalized by the teacher's per-batch std, stop-grad on teacher. Total loss = 1*L_teacher + 1*L_student + gamma*L_KD (gamma=1 GPT-2, gamma=20 LLaMA-1B because the distill loss magnitude shrinks). Supervision is trajectory-level: nothing constrains individual latents; the read-out interface at the answer position is what gets aligned.
papers.measured_result: GSM8k GPT-2: 43.7% vs CoT-SFT ~44% (99% of explicit CoT; first implicit method to match it at that scale), Coconut 34.1%, iCoT 30.1%, No-CoT 19.1%; 3.1x compression (8.2x on verbose NL CoTs, where CODI BEATS CoT-SFT). LLaMA-1B: 90% of CoT-SFT. OOD (GPT-2): SVAMP 42.9/GSM-Hard 9.9/MultiArith 92.8, beating CoT-SFT on all three. KILLER ABLATIONS: remove the L1 distill loss -> 24.5% (near No-CoT: latent info present but generation cannot use it, i.e., exactly the HLWM failure signature); keep the final CoT step in teacher -> 31.7%; remove projection -> 42.5%; independent static teacher -> 27.1%.

papers.title: SIM-CoT: Supervised Implicit Chain-of-Thought
papers.scale_tested: GPT-2, LLaMA-3.2 1B/3B, LLaMA-3.1 8B; GSM8k-Aug 385k rows; plug-in on Coconut (full FT, lr 1e-4, curriculum) and on CODI (LoRA r=128 alpha=32 per released scripts: 1B lr 8e-4 10 epochs, batch 64x2 accum, distill_loss_factor 20); auxiliary decoder = full architectural copy of the backbone, training-only
papers.core_mechanism: Step-level supervision on EACH latent token: an auxiliary decoder takes latent z_k alone as a prefix embedding and must autoregressively GENERATE the k-th gold reasoning-step text via CE (L_step); total loss adds L_step (explain_loss_factor=1.0 in released code) to the backbone's answer CE (+ CODI's distill loss when stacked on CODI). Decoder discarded at inference (zero overhead). Diagnosis motivating it: scaling Coconut past 4-5 latents collapses; collapsed runs show inter-latent L2 shrinking 28.3 -> 4.2 while latents drift AWAY from the vocab-embedding center (36.2 -> 39.4), latents homogenize into numbers-only and lose operator info. Step supervision restores inter-latent distance to 32.8 and stabilizes 8-16 latent training. Also notes CODI's KL/distill anchor is what prevents catastrophic forgetting at >=1B.
papers.measured_result: GPT-2: Coconut+SIM-CoT 44.8% (+8.2 over Coconut, +2.1 over explicit SFT-CoT at 2.3x token efficiency); CODI+SIM-CoT +0.6 only (42.6). LLaMA-1B: CODI+SIM-CoT 56.1% (+3.4, = 96% of SFT-CoT 58.4); 3B +1.5; 8B +3.0 (64.1). Decoder must match backbone scale: 1B decoder on 1B backbone best; 3B/8B decoders DEGRADE (50.4/50.0 vs 56.1).

papers.title: CoLaR: Think Silently, Think Fast: Dynamic Latent Compression of LLM Reasoning Chains
papers.scale_tested: FROZEN LLaMA-3.2-1B-Instruct and frozen DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B + trainable LoRA r=128 alpha=32 + 3-layer MLP latent head (d=2048); GSM8k-Aug 385k (SFT: batch 256, lr 1e-4, up to 50 epochs or 12h on 8x A100) and MATH with only 7.5k training rows; RL (GRPO, group 8, lr 1e-6, binary reward, no KL) on 1x A100; also scaled to LLaMA-8B
papers.core_mechanism: Latents ARE compressed gold-trace embeddings: sample compression factor c in [1,5] per step, merge c consecutive gold reasoning-token embeddings by sum/sqrt(c) (mean-pooling distorts the distribution and costs 2-3 pts), normalize targets by the embedding std (~0.02 Llama / ~0.03 Qwen). Two dense losses, fully parallel/teacher-forced: (1) L_comp = CE where each compressed position must predict a token uniformly sampled from its c-token group, plus answer CE — dense token supervision through the latent positions; (2) L_latent = latent head regresses next compressed embedding (soft-MSE + entropy bonus, or Gaussian NLL for hard tasks). Probabilistic latent head enables GRPO post-training over sampled latent chains with per-token averaged advantage.
papers.measured_result: GSM8k-Aug: CoLaR-2 48.8% (only -4.8 vs explicit CoT) at 53% chain-length reduction; CoLaR-5 +14.1% average over Coconut with fewer steps (4.57 vs 6.00). KILLER ABLATION CoLaR-OC (answer-only CE, no compressed-token CE): -1.6/-0.6 pts — 'dense reasoning supervision signals are crucial'. MATH at 7.5k rows: Qwen-1.5B 8.94% -> ~14.3% with GRPO, -82.8% latent chain length; Llama-1B weaker and RL near-collapse without reward averaging. 8B+RL: GPQA 37.5% > 35.7% CoT teacher.

papers.title: Coconut: Training Large Language Models to Reason in a Continuous Latent Space
papers.scale_tested: GPT-2 124M (and 1B in reproductions); GSM8k-Aug 385k; full fine-tune, multi-stage curriculum replacing CoT steps with latents (3 epochs/stage + 15 final), lr 1e-4
papers.core_mechanism: Last hidden state fed back as next input embedding; supervision is ANSWER-ONLY (latents unconstrained) plus curriculum that starts from explicit CoT. The canonical weak-supervision baseline.
papers.measured_result: GSM8k GPT-2 34.1-36.6% — 8-10 pts below explicit CoT; collapses when scaled to 5+ latents (to 12.5% in SIM-CoT's replication); every successor paper's ablations show answer-only supervision is the failure mode. This is the published version of HLWM's channel failure.

papers.title: CCoT: Compressed Chain of Thought: Efficient Reasoning through Dense Representations
papers.scale_tested: LLaMA2-7B-Chat, ~9,000 GSM8k instances (explicitly contrasted with 385k-row methods as data-efficient), two LoRA modules (CCOT generator + DECODE reader) trained successively, layerwise hidden-state approximation training
papers.core_mechanism: Latent targets are ACTUAL hidden states of the gold CoT: precompute hidden states of Q+gold-chain+A, a linear scorer selects a subset (ratio r) of chain positions, CCOT module is trained layer-by-layer to autoregressively approximate those selected hidden states; then a separate DECODE adapter learns to answer conditioned on query + generated contemplation tokens (compressed chains are out-of-distribution for the frozen base — a dedicated reader adapter is REQUIRED); a binary end-classifier handles variable length; unfreezing only post-autoregressive-layer generator params during decode training helps.
papers.measured_result: GSM8k EM: r=0.10 -> 0.179 at 0.78s/answer vs full-chain 0.315 at 8.10s and pause-tokens 0.092; roughly doubles the no-CoT baseline (~0.09) at 10x compression. The only datapoint in this lineage at HLWM's DATA scale (~9k rows) — gains are real but roughly half of explicit CoT retained.

papers.title: SoftCoT: Soft Chain-of-Thought for Efficient Reasoning with LLMs
papers.scale_tested: FROZEN LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct / Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct backbones; small frozen assistant model generates instance-specific soft thought tokens; ONLY a projection module is trained; 5 reasoning benchmarks
papers.core_mechanism: Sidesteps catastrophic forgetting by freezing everything except a projection that maps assistant-generated soft tokens into the backbone's representation space; CE through the frozen backbone trains the projection — evidence that a frozen decoder CAN learn to consume projected continuous thoughts if the CE gradient flows through the consumption interface.
papers.measured_result: Modest but consistent gains (~+0.5-2 pts over zero-shot CoT at 7-8B; variance reduction with self-consistency). Not tested below 7B; gains too small to carry a headline claim alone.

papers.title: From Explicit CoT to Implicit CoT: Learning to Internalize CoT Step by Step (iCoT)
papers.scale_tested: GPT-2 and up; GSM8k-Aug 385k; full fine-tune, token-removal curriculum (4-16 tokens/epoch)
papers.core_mechanism: Stepwise internalization: progressively delete CoT tokens during fine-tuning so hidden states absorb the computation; no latent tokens at all.
papers.measured_result: GPT-2 30.1% GSM8k; FAILS to scale to LLaMA-1B (19.0%, below No-CoT 28.8%) — curriculum forgetting; motivated CODI's single-stage design.

papers.title: Do Latent Tokens Think? A Causal and Adversarial Analysis of Chain-of-Continuous-Thought
papers.scale_tested: Coconut-trained models; steering/perturbation + bias/OOD shortcut tests on MMLU and HotpotQA
papers.core_mechanism: Adversarial audit: steer/perturb latent tokens vs explicit CoT tokens; measure sensitivity and shortcut exploitation under biased and OOD splits.
papers.measured_result: Coconut latents show minimal steering sensitivity (not reasoning-critical) and the models consistently exploit dataset artifacts — 'pseudo-reasoning': benchmark gains without causal latent use. Direct vindication of HLWM's masked-premise/shuffled-prefix necessity gates as the primary metric.

papers.title: How Do Latent Reasoning Methods Perform Under Weak and Strong Supervision?
papers.scale_tested: Systematic comparison across Coconut/CODI/SIM-CoT-style supervision levels (small-model regime)
papers.core_mechanism: Varies supervision strength on latent tokens and measures shortcut reliance and latent hypothesis diversity.
papers.measured_result: Pervasive shortcut behavior across all methods (high accuracy without latent reasoning); stronger step-level supervision MITIGATES shortcuts but collapses the latents' ability to hold multiple hypotheses; no faithful BFS-style search found. Implication for v10: dense supervision is the right tool for proving the channel works, but pair it with attribution controls, and don't also claim exploration/diversity from the same latents.

lenses.recipe: DIAGNOSIS FIRST: HLWM's probe-0.30/generation-0.00 channel is the exact published failure of answer-only supervision (Coconut; CODI's 'w/o L1' ablation drops 43.7->24.5; CoLaR-OC ablation; SIM-CoT's homogenization+vocab-drift geometry, which also matches lanes' cosine 0.94-0.98). The literature's fix is unanimous: put a dense loss ON THE GENERATION-SIDE INTERFACE, and keep latents inside the embedding distribution. V10 recipe: (0) DATA: emit gold step-by-step traces for every synthetic row in GSM8k-Aug style (structured minimal steps, e.g. '<<a op b = c>>'); ALWAYS EXCLUDE the final answer-producing step from the teacher trace (CODI: keeping it costs 12 pts via copy shortcut). (1) ARCHITECTURE: one shared LoRA (keep r16 all-layers; CODI/CoLaR used r128 a32 — raise rank only if throughput allows) serving both teacher and student passes; K=4-6 latent tokens, NOT 42 (all successful systems use 3-13; CODI peaks at 6; long latent chains are the collapse regime); 2-layer MLP+LayerNorm projection on each latent before re-injection (+1.2 pts in CODI); latents/targets normalized by the base embedding std (Qwen ~0.02-0.03, CoLaR) so the prefix lives in embedding space — this also structurally attacks the v6/v8 register/scaffold pathology. (2) LOSSES, single stage, no curriculum (CODI: curriculum forgetting is why Coconut/iCoT lose 10-20 pts): L = 1.0*L_teacher(CE on Q+trace+A through same LoRA) + 1.0*L_student(CE on answer after latents) + gamma*L_KD(smooth-L1 between student and teacher hidden states at the pre-answer token, all layers, per-layer /teacher-batch-std, stop-grad teacher; gamma=1 initially, raise toward 20 if distill/CE loss ratio is small — LLaMA-1B needed 20) + 1.0*L_step(SIM-CoT: auxiliary decoder = the SAME frozen base with its own LoRA, conditioned on z_k alone as prefix embedding, CE to generate gold step k; drop at inference) + CoLaR grounding for most of the budget: teacher-force latents as compressed gold-trace embeddings (sum of c consecutive token embeddings / sqrt(c), c sampled in [1,3]) with (a) CE at each compressed position on a token sampled from its c-group and (b) an MLP latent head regressing the next compressed embedding (soft-MSE; targets std-normalized). The CoLaR path is fully parallel (no sequential latent decode) — it is the only variant whose training cost fits a T4 budget; run CODI-style free-running student passes on only ~25% of steps. (3) LANES/EXPERTS: give each lane its own SIM-CoT decode target = a distinct gold sub-trace section (premise extraction / computation / unit-format check); per-lane decode CE makes cosine-0.95 collapse impossible without the loss exploding; gate on SIM-CoT's collapse metrics (inter-latent L2, latent-to-vocab-center distance) — collapsed runs sit at L2~4 vs healthy ~28-33. (4) OPTIMIZER: AdamW wd 0.1, cosine + 3% warmup, max-grad-norm 2.0, lr 5e-4-8e-4 for LoRA at 0.6B, effective batch >=64 via grad accum (batch-4 is far below every published recipe and the KD std-normalization is batch-statistics-based). (5) GATES: keep v9's masked-premise + within-family shuffled-prefix necessity controls as the headline (2512.21711/2602.22441 show accuracy alone is confounded by shortcuts); add CODI's interpretability probe (decode each latent through the LM head; healthy models match reference intermediate results 75-97%).
lenses.feasibility_at_our_budget: Partially supported — the MODEL scale is the well-replicated part, the DATA/COMPUTE scale is an extrapolation. In favor: CODI works at GPT-2 (124M, 5x smaller than Qwen3-0.6B) and 1B THROUGH LoRA (r128 a32, released scripts confirm use_lora=True); CoLaR is explicitly FROZEN-1B-base + LoRA + external latent head — the precise HLWM architecture class — and its SFT losses are teacher-forced/parallel, so cost scales like ordinary SFT; CCoT got real (if halved) gains from only ~9k rows via LoRA adapters, the single small-data datapoint; HLWM's synthetic families (chain 1-3, exact gold traces) are far easier than GSM8k, so 6 latents and 10-20 epochs over 7.5k rows (~100-150k example-presentations) is plausibly enough where GSM8k needed 15M. Against: every headline number used 385k rows and 36-48 A100-hours (CODI-GPT2 alone is ~20-40x the 6.5 T4-hour budget in raw FLOPs-hours); nobody has published this recipe at 0.6B + <=50k rows + <7 GPU-h simultaneously; the SIM-CoT auxiliary decoder adds ~1.5-2x training FLOPs and ~1.2GB bf16 weights (fits 2xT4 at 0.6B, but budget the throughput test first); CODI's KD normalization and batch-128 assumption degrade at grad-accum-4; and CoLaR's one true small-data run (MATH 7.5k) produced weak absolute numbers on a hard task. Verdict: the mechanism transfer (dense generation-side supervision fixes probe-decodable-but-unusable latents) is strongly evidenced and is the single best-matched fix in the literature for HLWM's exact failure signature; expect it to move masked-row accuracy off 0.000 on easy synthetic families, but a CODI-magnitude result (99% of explicit CoT) at this budget is NOT evidenced anywhere — pre-register a modest gate (masked-channel accuracy > No-CoT control by a fixed margin) rather than parity with explicit CoT.
risks: Data/compute extrapolation: all headline results use 385k rows and 36-48 A100-h; the only <=9k-row datapoint (CCoT, 7B) retained roughly half of explicit-CoT performance — at 0.6B with 6.5 T4-h the honest expectation is 'clearly above No-CoT', not parity.

Shortcut contamination: 2512.21711 and 2602.22441 show latent-token methods pervasively pass benchmarks without causally using the latents; if v10 drops the masked-premise/shuffled-prefix necessity gates, a 'working' channel could be another pseudo-reasoning artifact.

Supervision-strength trade-off (2602.22441): strong per-step supervision that fixes the channel simultaneously collapses latent hypothesis diversity — the lanes may become distinct only as relays of the gold trace; keep the trained-gist/attribution control, and do not stack an exploration/diversity claim on the same latents.

Marginal value ordering: SIM-CoT on top of an already-working CODI gave only +0.6 at GPT-2 (vs +8.2 on broken Coconut) — if budget forces a choice, CODI-KD + CoLaR grounding is the core; SIM-CoT decode is best spent where collapse is the failure (lanes), not stacked everywhere.

Qwen3-0.6B specifics: no-BOS/eos aliasing and RMSNorm scale-invariance killed prior HLWM gates; CODI's KD relies on per-layer std normalization with batch statistics (fragile at grad-accum 4) and its gamma needed a 20x adjustment between GPT-2 and 1B — plan a short calibration run to set gamma by loss-magnitude ratio before the main 3200 steps.

Sequential latent decode cost: CODI/SIM-CoT free-running student passes add K+2 extra forwards per example on T4s with no flash-attention; if throughput measurement shows <0.6 steps/s, fall back to CoLaR teacher-forced grounding for 100% of steps (its -OC ablation shows only ~1.6 pts lost vs the full recipe at 385k rows, and it is the frozen-base-verified variant).

lenses.lens: Curriculum internalization of reasoning (Coconut stage schedules, ICoT-SI token-by-token removal, ICoT-KD vertical distillation, pause/filler tokens, Quiet-STaR, CODI self-distillation)

papers.title: Training Large Language Models to Reason in a Continuous Latent Space (Coconut)
papers.scale_tested: GPT-2 124M main; Llama-3.2-3B & Llama-3-8B appendix. Data: GSM8k-Aug 385,620 train rows; ProntoQA 9,000; ProsQA 17,886. Batch 128, lr 1e-4, up to 50 epochs (GSM8K: 6 ep initial + 3 ep/stage x 4 stages; logic: 5 ep/stage x 7 stages). n+1 sequential forward passes for n latents.
papers.core_mechanism: Stage curriculum: at stage k, first k language CoT steps replaced by k*c continuous thoughts (last hidden state recycled as next input embedding, <bot>/<eot> delimiters). c=2 for GSM8K, c=1 for logic. CE loss only on remaining text (masked on latents). Optimizer state reset at every stage switch. Fully off-policy/teacher-forced.
papers.measured_result: GSM8k: Coconut 34.1 vs explicit CoT 42.9 (REGRESSION -8.8), No-CoT 16.5, iCoT 30.0, pause-token 16.4. w/o curriculum 14.4 (= worse than No-CoT: curriculum is the whole effect). pause-as-thought WITH curriculum 24.1. ProsQA 97.0 vs CoT 77.5; ProntoQA 99.8. c=3 causes loss spikes at stage transitions. Llama-3B: 31.7 vs no-CoT 26.0; 8B: 43.6 vs 42.2 (gains shrink with scale).

papers.title: From Explicit CoT to Implicit CoT: Learning to Internalize CoT Step by Step (ICoT-SI)
papers.scale_tested: GPT-2 Small 117M / Medium, Phi-3 3.8B, Mistral-7B. Data: 808k rows per multiplication task; GSM8K-Aug 378k. Batch 32, lr 5e-5 (2e-5..1e-5 for 3.8B/7B), up to 200 epochs or 24h on 1x H100 80GB.
papers.core_mechanism: Token-by-token removal: linear schedule s(t)=floor(Delta*t/T) CoT tokens removed from the LEFT per epoch (Delta=8 mult, Delta=1 GSM8K/GPT-2), plus Removal Smoothing (random extra offset o, P(o) ~ exp(-4o), i.e. 2% of batches remove >=1 extra token) and full AdamW optimizer-state reset at each removal. Off-policy.
papers.measured_result: GPT-2 Small: 9x9 mult 0.99 (No-CoT 0.00; ICoT-KD fails at 5x5=0.10). GSM8K: GPT-2 Small 0.30, Medium 0.35, Mistral-7B 0.51 vs explicit CoT 0.68. Ablations: Delta=16 diverges permanently; no smoothing or no optimizer-reset -> accuracy drops to 0 and never recovers; Fig 4: two identical runs differing only in seed, one permanently fails. Right-side removal much worse.

papers.title: Implicit Chain of Thought Reasoning via Knowledge Distillation (ICoT-KD)
papers.scale_tested: GPT-2 Small/Medium; same 808k multiplication / 385k GSM8k-Aug data regime.
papers.core_mechanism: Teacher trained on explicit CoT; student distills teacher's hidden states 'vertically' across layers so reasoning happens in the layer stack instead of horizontal token emission; separate emulator model.
papers.measured_result: 4x4 mult 0.97 (GPT-2 Small) but 5x5 collapses to 0.10; GSM8K 0.20/0.22 (Small/Medium). Superseded by ICoT-SI and CODI on every benchmark.

papers.title: Think before you speak: Training language models with pause tokens
papers.scale_tested: 1B and 130M decoder-only models PRETRAINED from scratch on 200B C4 tokens with 10% pause insertion; then finetuned per task.
papers.core_mechanism: Learnable <pause> tokens appended; answer extraction delayed until last pause; CE loss skipped on pause positions. Four regimes crossing pause-in-pretraining x pause-in-finetuning.
papers.measured_result: PausePT_PauseFT (1B): SQuAD EM 36.4->55.9, CSQA +~8, GSM8k 7.5->8.5, gains on 8/9 tasks. CRITICAL NEGATIVE for us: StdPT_PauseFT (pause introduced only at finetuning, the only regime available on a frozen pretrained base) is 'lukewarm' — GSM8k 6.9-8.0 vs 7.5 baseline, i.e. no gain or a loss. Content-free compute tokens added at finetune time do ~nothing.

papers.title: Let's Think Dot by Dot: Hidden Computation in Transformer Language Models (filler tokens)
papers.scale_tested: 34M Llama (4 layers, d=384, 6 heads) trained FROM SCRATCH on synthetic 3SUM/2SUM (algorithmic data, effectively unlimited rows).
papers.core_mechanism: Meaningless filler tokens ('...') in place of CoT give parallel compute width; theory: helps only for problems within TC0 with quantifier depth >2 that admit PARALLEL decompositions.
papers.measured_result: Length-12 3SUM: 100% with fillers vs 66% (near-random) without, no-filler trained 5x longer. Key negative: learning to USE fillers required dense supervision — training traces containing instance-adaptive parallel decompositions; standard sequential CoT data was insufficient to induce filler use. Frozen final-layer probes decode the hidden computation.

papers.title: Quiet-STaR: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Think Before Speaking
papers.scale_tested: Mistral-7B, continued pretraining on OpenWebMath + C4; ~16 sampled thoughts of ~12 tokens at EVERY token position; trained on one node of 8x H100 80GB.
papers.core_mechanism: On-policy: tokenwise-parallel sampling of rationales, mixing head to blend with/without-thought logits, non-myopic multi-token teacher-forced loss, REINFORCE on rationale quality. The only method in this lens that requires on-policy sampling.
papers.measured_result: Zero-shot GSM8K 5.9->10.9, CommonsenseQA 36.3->47.2 with no task finetuning. Compute multiplies forward cost by n_thoughts (~16x); no result below 7B exists. Infeasible at 0.6B/T4/6.5h by ~2 orders of magnitude.

papers.title: CODI: Compressing Chain-of-Thought into Continuous Space via Self-Distillation
papers.scale_tested: GPT-2 124M and LLaMA-3.2-1B-Instruct, both with LoRA r=128 alpha=32 (bf16). Data: GSM8k-Aug 385k (+GSM8k-Aug-NL; CSQA-CoT 8.1k). Batch 128, cosine+3% warmup. GPT-2: lr 3e-3, 40 epochs, ~36h on 1x A100 80GB. LLaMA-1B: lr 8e-4, teacher weight gamma=20, 10 epochs, ~48h A100.
papers.core_mechanism: SINGLE-STAGE replacement for the multi-stage curriculum: one shared model jointly trained as teacher (CE on gold CoT) and student (CE on answer given question + 6 recycled-hidden-state continuous thoughts), coupled by L_KD = L1 distance between teacher and student hidden states ACROSS ALL LAYERS at one designated answer-cue token. L = alpha*L_student + beta*L_KD + gamma*L_teacher (alpha=beta=1; raise beta to ~5 / gamma to ~20 at 1B because distill-loss magnitude is ~10x smaller). No optimizer resets, no stages, off-policy.
papers.measured_result: GSM8k GPT-2: 43.7% = 99% of explicit CoT-SFT (44.1%), +28.2% absolute over Coconut, 3.1x token compression; No-CoT-SFT 19.1%. LLaMA-1B reaches 90% of CoT-SFT. Ablations: w/o L1 loss 24.5% (the dense hidden-state supervision IS the mechanism); separate frozen teacher 27.1% (self-shared weights essential); accuracy peaks at exactly 6 continuous thoughts, degrades beyond. Beats CoT-SFT OOD (SVAMP/GSM-Hard/MultiArith).

papers.title: Do Latent Tokens Think? A Causal and Adversarial Analysis of Chain-of-Continuous-Thought
papers.scale_tested: Analysis of Coconut-style trained models (GPT-2-scale Coconut checkpoints); steering + bias/OOD evaluations on MMLU, HotpotQA.
papers.core_mechanism: Steering perturbations of latent vs CoT tokens; shortcut probes under answer-position bias and spurious-context injection.
papers.measured_result: Coconut latent tokens show minimal sensitivity to steering (placeholder-like, not reasoning-critical) and the models exploit dataset artifacts, inflating benchmarks without genuine reasoning. Directly motivates keeping HLWM's shuffled-prefix / masked-premise necessity controls as primary gates for any v10 latent channel.

lenses.recipe: V10 CHANNEL RECIPE — replace the workspace-projection interface with CODI-style self-distilled continuous thoughts; use the ICoT-SI curriculum only as a secondary arm. (1) DATA: for every synthetic row emit a GOLD compact CoT in equation style (GSM8k-Aug format, e.g. '<<12*4=48>><<48+3=51>>'), <=24 CoT tokens — CODI shows compact CoT internalizes better than verbose NL, and short chains are what make our step budget plausible. Expand rows toward 30-50k if wall-clock allows: data exposure, not method, is the binding constraint. (2) ARCHITECTURE: delete workspace projections, scalar gates, and KL-to-base entirely (Coconut/CODI use none; HLWM's gates were provably inert and KL closed the channel). Continuous thought = the model's own last-layer hidden state at position t fed back as the input embedding at t+1, after a <bot> embedding; exactly 6 thoughts then <eot> then answer (CODI's peak; Coconut c=3-at-once destabilizes). Costs n+1=7 sequential forwards on a short sequence — budget-check on T4, expect ~2-3x step cost. (3) LOSS (single stage, all 3200 steps, one shared LoRA'd model playing both roles per batch): L = 1.0*CE_student(answer | Q, 6 latents) + beta*L1(h_student, h_teacher, all layers, at the answer-cue token) + gamma*CE_teacher(gold CoT + answer | Q). Start beta=1, gamma=1; per CODI's 1B findings sweep beta in {1,5} and gamma in {1,20} so the three terms are the same order of magnitude by step ~100 (at 1B the distill loss is ~10x smaller). Mask CE on latent positions. (4) OPTIMIZATION: LoRA all layers — raise rank toward 64-128 if VRAM allows (CODI used r128; r16 is untested for moving hidden states enough to satisfy the L1 target); lr 8e-4 (CODI's 1B value) cosine with 3% warmup, AdamW, bf16. (5) OPTIONAL CURRICULUM ARM (only if the CODI arm shows life in a smoke run): stage 0 = 800 steps explicit-CoT SFT, then step-denominated ICoT-SI left-side removal, Delta = 1 gold token per ~100-130 steps (all ~24 tokens gone by step ~2600), removal smoothing lambda=4 (P(extra removal)~2%), full optimizer-state reset at each removal, never >2 tokens per transition. (6) NO ON-POLICY SAMPLING: every method that worked at 117M-1B (Coconut, ICoT-SI, ICoT-KD, CODI) is fully teacher-forced; the only on-policy method (Quiet-STaR) needed 8xH100 at 7B. Keep training entirely off-policy; keep the existing conformal-abstention heads on top unchanged. (7) GATES: target 'latent >= No-CoT + margin and >= 0.6x explicit-CoT-SFT', NOT CoT parity (Coconut regressed -8.8 on GSM8K even at 385k rows); keep masked-premise rows, within-family shuffled-latent control, and latent-ablation arm as primary necessity gates (2512.21711 shows Coconut latents can be placeholders riding shortcuts). EXPERTS/LANES under this lens: give each lane a DIFFERENT contiguous slice of the gold CoT as its distillation target (lane 1 <- steps 1..k hidden states, lane 2 <- steps k+1..m), i.e. dense per-lane supervision instead of emergent diversity — literature-consistent (it is per-token L1 supervision a la CODI) but untested anywhere; treat as exploratory, not preregistered-headline.
lenses.feasibility_at_our_budget: SPLIT VERDICT. Model scale: YES — this is the one literature family genuinely replicated BELOW our size: GPT-2 117-124M (Coconut, ICoT-SI, ICoT-KD, CODI — 4 independent groups) and LLaMA-3.2-1B (CODI), bracketing Qwen3-0.6B; LoRA-only training is proven (CODI r128). Off-policy: YES — no successful sub-7B method needs on-policy sampling. Data/compute: NO published success anywhere near our exposure. All positive results used 378k-808k rows x 10-200 epochs (CODI GPT-2: 385k x 40 ep = ~15M row-visits, 36 A100-hours; ICoT-SI: up to 24 H100-hours; Coconut ProntoQA, the smallest: 9k rows x ~50 ep = 450k visits). Our envelope is 7.5-50k rows x ~1-2 epochs = 12.8k-100k row-visits on T4s — 5-1000x less. Mitigating factors, honestly weighed: our families are algorithmically uniform synthetic templates (closer to Pfau's 3SUM and Deng's multiplication, where small models internalized fully, than to GSM8K), gold CoT is ~24 tokens not 150, and CODI removes the curriculum's stage/step-count dependence entirely (no per-stage epoch requirement, no optimizer resets), which is why it — not token-by-token ICoT-SI — is the only variant with a credible shot in 3200 steps. A token-by-token internalization curriculum IS schedulable inside 3200 steps (24 tokens at Delta=1/100 steps) but each removal then gets ~100 gradient updates vs ~25,000/epoch in the paper — high risk of the documented non-recovering collapse. Realistic expectation even on success: latent channel lands between No-CoT and explicit CoT (Coconut -8.8 GSM8K; Mistral ICoT-SI 0.51 vs 0.68), so preregister the gate as necessity + margin-over-No-CoT, not CoT parity. Pause-token evidence is a direct warning: extra compute tokens added at finetune time on a standard-pretrained base give ~nothing unless anchored to gold CoT content — which is exactly what the CODI L1 term provides and what all previous HLWM latent prefixes lacked.
risks: Data-exposure gap: every published success used >=378k rows and 10-200 epochs (>=450k row-visits); our max is ~100k visits — an untested regime where the most likely failure is silent underfit of the L1 distillation target, not instability.

Seed-dependent permanent collapse at removal/stage transitions: ICoT-SI Fig 4 shows two identical runs where one seed never recovers; with HLWM's 2-seed replication bar this is a first-order risk for the curriculum arm (less so for single-stage CODI).

Internalization ceiling below explicit CoT (Coconut GSM8K 34.1 vs 42.9; ICoT-SI Mistral 0.51 vs 0.68): if v10 gates demand CoT parity the study fails by construction — gate on necessity + margin over No-CoT instead.

LoRA rank mismatch: CODI's only LoRA evidence is r=128; HLWM's r=16 may lack capacity to move all-layer hidden states onto the teacher's manifold; budget a rank bump or expect the L1 loss to plateau high.

Pseudo-reasoning shortcut confound (arXiv:2512.21711): Coconut-style latents can be steering-insensitive placeholders that ride dataset artifacts — the within-family shuffled-prefix and masked-premise controls must stay primary gates, and a passing channel that fails the shuffle control must be reported as shortcut, not success.

Throughput: 6 recycled thoughts = 7 sequential forwards per student row plus a teacher forward (~2-3x current step cost on T4); at fixed 6.5h this either cuts steps below 3200 or forces shorter sequences — measure before preregistering step count.

lenses.lens: Posterior collapse theory and fixes, mapped from text VAEs onto HLWM's setting: per-input latent prefix + frozen 0.6B decoder + LM loss, where the decoder can always ignore the prefix. Core diagnosis via Wang/Blei/Cunningham: collapse is not (only) an optimization accident — the posterior collapses iff the latent is NON-IDENTIFIABLE in the generative model. On every unmasked HLWM row, frozen Qwen + LoRA already models p(answer|prompt) without the prefix, so the ignore-the-prefix solution is a global optimum, not a bad local one; sprinkling 99-405 masked rows into 7.5k leaves the average gradient dominated by rows where the prefix is useless. Second diagnosis via He et al. (lagging inference): even when masking makes the latent identifiable, the decoder path (LoRA) adapts faster than the encoder learns to emit decoder-legible codes, so the decoder commits to ignoring garbage embeddings early — consistent with HLWM's probe result (info present, ~0.30 decodable) with 0.000 generative use: the encoder never received a dense training signal THROUGH the decoder interface. Third: HLWM's KL-to-base anchor is exactly the beta-pressure that theory says closes the channel (it penalizes any output distribution shift the prefix causes) — the in-house v8 finding that it pushed the channel shut is the textbook prediction. The fixes with real evidence sort into four families: (a) minimum-usage constraints (free bits, delta-VAE) → a hinged 'usage floor' loss on the logprob gap between true-prefix and shuffled-prefix conditioning; (b) dense direct supervision of the latent (bag-of-words aux loss, ICAE autoencoding) → make the frozen decoder reconstruct the premise from the prefix alone; (c) structural necessity (Bowman word dropout, gisting attention masks) → the decoder's attention physically cannot see the premise, on 100% of rows, with a ramp rather than binary masking; (d) optimization scheduling (KL/cyclical annealing, aggressive encoder training) → encoder-first phases and re-freezing the decoder when the usage metric stalls. Critically, families (b) and (c) have strong evidence OUTSIDE the VAE family in exactly the frozen-decoder-plus-latent-prefix architecture (gist tokens, ICAE, xRAG), and family (c)+(d) at sub-1B scale (prefix-tuning at GPT-2 Medium 345M). The same non-identifiability lens explains expert/route collapse (router non-identifiable when one expert suffices) and lane collapse (lanes non-identifiable when their targets are identical): the fix is disjoint dense supervision targets per component, not diversity penalties (which HLWM measured to be inert three times, as theory predicts under collapse).

papers.title: Generating Sentences from a Continuous Space
papers.scale_tested: single-layer LSTM VAE (~10-20M params), PTB (~42k train sentences) and Books Corpus; hours on one GPU
papers.core_mechanism: KL cost annealing (weight 0→1) + word dropout / historyless decoding: replace a fraction of decoder input tokens with UNK so the decoder must consult the latent
papers.measured_result: Without tricks KL→0 (collapse to RNNLM); with annealing+word-dropout KL stays nonzero (~2% of total cost on PTB) at comparable PPL. Extreme 100%-dropout (fully historyless) decoder produces implausible text — total masking from step 0 is the known failure mode, matching HLWM v9's 0.000 masked accuracy

papers.title: Improved Variational Inference with Inverse Autoregressive Flow (free bits)
papers.scale_tested: CIFAR-10 ResNet VAE, ~1-10M params; free bits since replicated on many small text VAEs
papers.core_mechanism: Free bits: L = recon − Σ_j max(λ, KL_j) — KL term only penalized above a floor λ per latent group, reserving a minimum information quota the model can use for free
papers.measured_result: Enabled deep IAF-VAE to reach 3.11 bpd CIFAR-10 (then-SOTA among VAEs); free bits became the standard collapse guard (still used, e.g., 2025 'Free Transformer'). Known caveat (Chen et al., VLAE): non-smooth objective, sharp transition at the floor causes optimization instability

papers.title: InfoVAE: Balancing Learning and Inference in Variational Autoencoders
papers.scale_tested: MNIST-scale conv VAEs (<5M params)
papers.core_mechanism: Replace per-datapoint KL with aggregate-posterior divergence (MMD) + explicit mutual-information term, removing the ELBO's incentive to zero out per-example information
papers.measured_result: MMD-VAE variants keep latents active regardless of decoder flexibility, on-par or better on inference-quality metrics; evidence is image-only, small scale — weakest direct mapping to a deterministic prefix (maps only to matching prefix-embedding statistics to base embedding statistics, which HLWM's input-norm projections already approximate)

papers.title: Learning Discourse-level Diversity for Neural Dialog Models using CVAEs (bag-of-words loss)
papers.scale_tested: GRU CVAE (~10M params), Switchboard (~2,400 dialogs — SMALLER than HLWM's 7.5k rows)
papers.core_mechanism: Auxiliary non-autoregressive head predicts the bag of words of the target utterance directly from the latent — dense supervision that bypasses the autoregressive decoder's ability to ignore z
papers.measured_result: Plain CVAE: KL→0 (collapse); KL annealing alone: temporary fix; +BoW loss: KL non-trivial for the whole run, large recall gains. Independently replicated (BN-VAE paper arXiv:2004.12585, PLATO arXiv:1910.07931 adopts it as a pretraining objective). The single most replicated small-scale, small-data fix in this literature

papers.title: Avoiding Latent Variable Collapse With Generative Skip Models
papers.scale_tested: LSTM VAEs on Yahoo (100k docs), MLP/conv VAEs on MNIST/Omniglot
papers.core_mechanism: Skip connections injecting z into every decoder layer; proved via data-processing inequality that this increases MI(x, z)
papers.measured_result: Yahoo, 32-dim latent: VAE MI 0.002 with 0 active units → Skip-VAE MI 0.31; SA-VAE MI 4.98/14 AU → Skip-SA-VAE MI 7.47/32 AU at similar NLL. Maps to HLWM as: inject the latent as per-layer K/V (deep prefix) at all layers, not as 42 input-embedding tokens

papers.title: Preventing Posterior Collapse with delta-VAEs
papers.scale_tested: Large autoregressive decoders: LM1B text + CIFAR-10/ImageNet32 (then-SOTA likelihoods); industrial compute
papers.core_mechanism: Constrain the variational family so KL(q||p) ≥ δ by construction ('committed rate') — a structural floor rather than an objective penalty, keeping powerful decoders unweakened
papers.measured_result: Non-collapsed latents with full autoregressive decoders, SOTA CIFAR-10/ImageNet32 likelihood; text (LM1B) latents stay informative. Deterministic analog for HLWM: guarantee minimum prefix influence structurally (attention masking) rather than by penalty — penalties on a collapsed channel were measured inert in HLWM 3 times, as predicted

papers.title: Lagging Inference Networks and Posterior Collapse in Variational Autoencoders
papers.scale_tested: 1-layer 512-d LSTM VAE, 32-d latent; Yahoo/Yelp (100k docs), OMNIGLOT; single GPU, hours
papers.core_mechanism: Collapse driven by training DYNAMICS: encoder lags the moving true posterior early, so the decoder learns to ignore z first. Fix: aggressively update the encoder (inner loop to convergence) before each decoder update, until MI(x,z) stops rising, then revert to standard training
papers.measured_result: Yahoo: annealed VAE MI ≈ 0.0 → aggressive VAE MI ≈ 2.9-3.8 nats with equal-or-better NLL than SA-VAE at 2-3x less compute. Directly implementable as encoder-first phases + decoder re-freezing in HLWM; cost only in early training

papers.title: Posterior Collapse and Latent Variable Non-identifiability
papers.scale_tested: Theory (exact-inference proof) + PPCA/GMM + small VAEs on MNIST/Omniglot/text; LIDVAE with Brenier-map decoders
papers.core_mechanism: Proof: posterior collapses iff the latent is non-identifiable — i.e., the likelihood can be matched without the latent. Not specific to neural nets or approximate inference. Fix: make the latent-to-likelihood map injective (identifiable) by construction
papers.measured_result: LIDVAE avoids collapse where standard VAEs collapse, across synthetic + real datasets. For HLWM this is the governing theorem: any path that lets the frozen decoder compute the answer without the prefix (unmasked rows, label-family correlations, premise paraphrase in the instruction) makes ignore-the-prefix a GLOBAL optimum

papers.title: Learning to Compress Prompts with Gist Tokens
papers.scale_tested: LLaMA-7B (decoder-only) and FLAN-T5-XXL 11B; Alpaca+ ~130k instructions, ~3 epochs, 4xA100
papers.core_mechanism: STRUCTURAL NECESSITY outside VAEs: modify the attention mask so tokens after the gist positions cannot attend to the prompt — gist tokens (the LM's own hidden states at learned token positions, same network as decoder) become the only channel; trained with plain LM loss
papers.measured_result: 26x prompt compression at 45.8-49.7% win-rate vs uncompressed positive control (i.e., near parity); discrete/TF-IDF compression baselines near negative control. The channel works because (a) attention masking makes it necessary on every row and (b) the encoder is the LM itself, so codes are decoder-legible by construction — both properties HLWM's sidecar lacked

papers.title: In-context Autoencoder for Context Compression in a Large Language Model (ICAE)
papers.scale_tested: LLaMA-7B FROZEN decoder + LoRA-adapted encoder (same LLM); large Pile-based AE+LM pretraining, then ~instruction fine-tune; ~1% added params
papers.core_mechanism: Exactly HLWM's architecture (frozen decoder + LoRA + learned memory-slot prefix), trained with an AUTOENCODING objective (decoder must reconstruct the original context from the memory slots) plus LM continuation, then instruction fine-tuning
papers.measured_result: 4x compression: BLEU >95% reconstructing 500-token contexts from k=128 slots; k=32/64 degrade sharply (>15x compression fails); pretrained 8x ICAE matches non-pretrained 4x. Lesson: prefix-only reconstruction THROUGH the frozen decoder is trainable and is the load-bearing objective; keep compression ratio modest (HLWM: short premises into 32-42 slots is comfortably under 4x information-wise)

papers.title: xRAG: Extreme Context Compression for Retrieval-augmented Generation with One Token
papers.scale_tested: Mistral-7B and Mixtral-8x7B, BOTH frozen; only a 2-layer projector trained; ~1M-scale paraphrase pretraining + instruction tuning with self-distillation
papers.core_mechanism: Project a retrieval embedding into the LM's space as ONE token; train with self-distillation: student (doc-as-token) matches the token-level output distribution of the SAME frozen LM given the doc as text — dense per-token supervision of channel usage, no exploration needed
papers.measured_result: +10% avg over 6 knowledge tasks vs no-retrieval, matches uncompressed RAG on several datasets, 3.53x FLOPs reduction. Caution for HLWM: v9 already flipped its KL to a distillation teacher and still got 0.000 masked accuracy — distillation alone, into a sidecar-produced prefix at 0.6B/7.5k rows, is demonstrably insufficient; xRAG's working recipe pairs it with representation-space pretraining and ~100x more data

papers.title: Prefix-Tuning: Optimizing Continuous Prompts for Generation
papers.scale_tested: GPT-2 Medium 345M / Large 774M, FROZEN; E2E ~42k rows, WebNLG ~22k, DART; single-GPU scale — the closest published match to HLWM's budget
papers.core_mechanism: Continuous prefix injected as per-layer key/value pairs at EVERY layer (not input embeddings), reparameterized through a bottleneck MLP for stability; frozen LM, plain LM loss
papers.measured_result: 0.1% trainable params ≈ full fine-tuning on E2E/WebNLG/DART; beats fine-tuning in low-data regimes. Removing the MLP reparameterization significantly degrades results (confirmed theoretically, arXiv:2410.02200, ICLR 2025). Companion negative result: shallow input-level soft prompts (Lester et al., arXiv:2104.08691) only match fine-tuning near ~10B params and are weak below 1B; P-Tuning v2 (arXiv:2110.07602) shows deep per-layer injection is what rescues sub-1B scale

lenses.recipe: V10 CHANNEL = 'self-encoded gist prefix with reconstruction floor'. (1) ENCODER IS THE BASE LM, NOT A SIDECAR: append K=32 learned gist tokens after the premise; the latent = the LoRA'd base model's hidden states at those positions (gisting 2304.08467, ICAE 2307.06945 — both successes use the LM as its own encoder, making codes decoder-legible by construction; HLWM's custom workspace module has failed 10 studies). (2) DEEP INJECTION: project gist states to per-layer K/V prefixes at ALL 28 layers via a 2-layer bottleneck MLP (dim 1024→512→2*28*head_dim*K slices), zero-init only the LAST projection bias, NOT a scalar gate (skip-VAE 1807.04863: per-layer links provably raise MI; prefix-tuning 2101.00190 + 2410.02200: MLP reparameterization is required for stability at 345M; Lester 2104.08691: input-embedding-level injection is known-weak below 1B — this alone may explain part of the v6-v9 failures). (3) STRUCTURAL NECESSITY ON 100% OF ROWS via attention masking, not id deletion: premise ids stay in-sequence (so gist tokens can encode them) but answer-span tokens get an attention mask blocking the premise span at every layer (gisting's mechanism). Ramp it: premise-token visible fraction 1.0→0.0 linearly over steps 0-1500 (Bowman 1511.06349: 100% historyless from step 0 yields garbage — v9's binary masking was the known-bad extreme; partial word dropout is the replicated fix). After step 1500 every row is fully gist-mediated: no identifiability leak (Wang/Blei/Cunningham 2301.00537 — with any leak, ignoring the prefix is a GLOBAL optimum). (4) LOSSES per batch: L_task = LM loss on gold trace+answer under the mask (weight 1.0). L_AE = prefix-only reconstruction: same frozen decoder conditioned on gist K/V + fixed cue must reproduce the premise, teacher-forced (weight 1.0 for steps 0-1000, cosine to 0.3; ICAE evidence this is trainable and load-bearing; keep effective compression ≤4x — premises ≤128 tokens into 32 slots). L_bow = single linear head from mean gist state to vocab, multi-label CE on premise content words (weight 0.5; Zhao 1703.10960 — replicated on 2.4k dialogs, cheapest dense signal). L_floor = free-bits analog (Kingma 1606.04934): Δ = logp(gold | true gist) − logp(gold | within-family-shuffled gist); loss = softplus((λ−Δ)/τ) with λ=0.1 nats/answer-token, τ=0.05, weight 1.0, computed on every 4th batch to save compute (hinge=free-bits semantics: zero pressure once above floor; soft hinge avoids the known non-smoothness). L_distill (optional, every other batch, weight 0.5): token-level KL to the SAME LoRA model with premise visible, stop-grad teacher (xRAG 2405.13792) — but treat as secondary: v9 proved distillation alone insufficient. DELETE the KL-to-base fluency anchor entirely (it is beta-pressure that provably closes the channel; in-house v8 confirmed). (5) SCHEDULE (He 1901.05534): Stage A, steps 0-600: decoder-side LoRA frozen, train gist LoRA + projections on L_AE + L_bow only; gate: premise reconstruction token-acc ≥0.9 before Stage B (rung-0 gate — if the frozen decoder cannot read the premise back out of the prefix, nothing downstream can work; abort cheap). Stage B: joint, all losses. Monitor Δ (the floor gap) every 200 steps; if it declines two consecutive checks, re-freeze decoder LoRA for 100 steps (aggressive-encoder analog). If any annealed weight must revisit high pressure, use 2 cycles (cyclical annealing 1903.10145). (6) EXPERTS AND LANES by the same theorem — identifiable by construction, not penalties (three in-house inert-penalty results are the predicted outcome): router trained with CE on synthetic family labels (weight 0.3, anneal to 0 after step 2000; report both supervised-router and annealed-free routing entropy); lanes get DISJOINT dense targets — lane 1 reconstructs the extraction sub-trace, lane 2 the computation sub-trace (per-lane L_AE on disjoint gold spans, generatable for free from the synthetic pipeline); cosine similarity becomes a gate (<0.8), never a loss. (7) DATA: raise to 30-50k rows — synthetic gold traces are free and every non-VAE success used ≥100k; data is the cheapest lever. (8) BUDGET: extra passes = AE decode (teacher-forced, short), shuffled-prefix forward (grad through student only, every 4th step), distill teacher (no-grad, every 2nd step) ≈ 1.8-2.2x v9 per-step cost; fit 6.5h by cutting to ~2400 steps at 30k rows (more rows/fewer epochs beats more epochs/fewer rows under collapse pressure) and capping sequence length at 384.
lenses.feasibility_at_our_budget: Split verdict. FOR the channel: the strongest scale-matched evidence is prefix-tuning (arXiv:2101.00190) — a deep per-layer continuous prefix demonstrably steers a FROZEN 345M GPT-2 with 22-42k rows on one GPU, i.e., the decoder-side read-out mechanism HLWM needs is proven below 1B, at HLWM's data size, provided injection is per-layer K/V with MLP reparameterization (HLWM's input-level 42-token prefix sits on the wrong side of the Lester-2104.08691 scale cliff). The classic collapse fixes with direct evidence at or BELOW HLWM's scale are: BoW auxiliary loss (replicated at ~10M params, 2.4k dialogs), aggressive encoder scheduling (1-layer LSTM, 100k docs), word-dropout ramp (PTB), free-bits. So a v10 built on: LM-as-own-encoder gist states + deep K/V injection + prefix-only reconstruction gate + usage-floor hinge is plausibly within reach of 0.6B / 30-50k rows / 6.5 GPU-h, and the Stage-A reconstruction gate makes failure cheap and diagnostic (abort at ~1 GPU-h if AE acc <0.9). AGAINST: every published per-input content-carrying prefix success in the frozen-LM family (gisting, ICAE, xRAG) is at 7B+ with 100k-1M+ rows; nobody has shown ICAE-style reconstruction working at 0.6B, and HLWM's own v9 shows distillation-to-teacher alone fails at this scale. The honest expectation: premise RECONSTRUCTION from the prefix (the ICAE objective) should be achievable — the probe already finds 0.30 of the info, and reconstruction supervision is dense; whether reconstruction converts to masked-row TASK accuracy at 0.6B is genuinely open and is exactly what v10 would test. Experts/lanes under direct label/sub-trace supervision are low-risk (supervised classification and span reconstruction are easy at this scale) but the resulting claim weakens from 'emergent specialization' to 'trainable supervised specialization' — that re-scope should be preregistered.
risks: Scale cliff for soft conditioning: input-level soft tokens are weak below ~1B (Lester arXiv:2104.08691); if v10 keeps embedding-level injection instead of per-layer K/V with MLP reparameterization (P-Tuning v2 arXiv:2110.07602, arXiv:2410.02200), the literature predicts failure regardless of the loss stack.

No existence proof at 0.6B: gisting/ICAE/xRAG all used >=7B encoders-as-LM and 100k-1M+ rows; ICAE shows compression quality degrades sharply past ~4x — a 0.6B model may sit below the capability floor for per-input content prefixes even with perfect training signal. The Stage-A reconstruction gate (abort <0.9 token-acc at ~1 GPU-h) is the mitigation.

Distillation is already falsified in-house as a sole fix (v9 teacher-KL, masked acc 0.000); if v10's gains come only from adding it back, expect another null — reconstruction-through-decoder and attention-mask necessity are the load-bearing changes.

Identifiability leaks recreate the collapse optimum globally (arXiv:2301.00537): any residual path from premise to answer (instruction paraphrase, family-correlated answer priors — recurred 6x in HLWM as degenerate thresholds) must be audited before training; with a leak, all auxiliary losses are fighting a true optimum.

Free-bits-style floor hinge is non-smooth (Chen et al. VLAE critique) and the shuffled-prefix contrast adds a forward pass; oscillation near the floor plus 1.8-2.2x step cost can blow the 6.5h budget — soft hinge, every-4th-batch application, and 2400-step cap are needed, and the throughput estimate must be re-measured before committing.

Reconstruction != task transfer: ICAE needed diverse pretraining to avoid downstream hallucination despite near-lossless AE; passing the AE gate but failing masked task accuracy is a live outcome — preregister that split result as its own rung so a partial success cannot be spun either way.

lenses.lens: Evidence that soft prefixes can carry content and what makes decoders read them (gisting, AutoCompressors, ICAE, xRAG, 500xCompressor, Gist-COCO, gist-failure-mode study, plus small-scale latent-token evidence: Coconut/iCoT/RMT and the prompt-tuning scale caveat)

papers.title: Learning to Compress Prompts with Gist Tokens (gisting)
papers.scale_tested: LLaMA-7B (fully finetuned, NOT frozen) and FLAN-T5-XXL 11B; Alpaca+ 130,321 examples; 3000 steps @ batch 128 (~3 epochs); 4xA100-80GB, ~7h for LLaMA-7B
papers.core_mechanism: Insert k gist tokens between prompt and input; modify the attention mask so all post-gist tokens CANNOT attend to the prompt — the gist activations become the only path. Objective is plain instruction-tuning CE; no extra loss. Readability is forced because the correct output is unpredictable without the prompt content, and dense CE flows through the gist positions on every token of every example.
papers.measured_result: Up to 26x prompt compression with 1 gist token; ROUGE-L/ChatGPT-judged quality within a few points of the positive control (same model, unmasked); 40% FLOPs reduction. Negative control (no prompt access) clearly worse — content demonstrably passes through the gist bottleneck.

papers.title: In-context Autoencoder for Context Compression in a Large Language Model (ICAE)
papers.scale_tested: Llama-7B decoder FROZEN; encoder = same LLM + LoRA + 128 memory-token embeddings (~1% added params). Pretrain on the Pile: 200k updates @ batch 256 (bf16, 8xA100-80GB), lr 1e-4; instruction FT on PwC 240k samples, 30k updates, lr 5e-5
papers.core_mechanism: Two pretraining objectives THROUGH the memory slots: (1) autoencoding — decoder must regenerate the original context token-by-token conditioned only on the 128 slots + an [AE] task token; (2) LM continuation from the slots. Then instruction FT (context, prompt, response). Frozen decoder reads the slots because hundreds of teacher-forced CE terms per example are satisfiable only via the slots.
papers.measured_result: 4x compression: near 100% BLEU/EM reconstruction for contexts ≤300 tokens; median BLEU >0.98 at 512-token contexts (EM ~0.6); reconstruction cross-entropy <0.05. Frozen 7B decoder demonstrably decodes content it never saw in text.

papers.title: Adapting Language Models to Compress Contexts (AutoCompressors)
papers.scale_tested: OPT-1.3B/2.7B fine-tuned on 2B Pile tokens; Llama-2-7B on 15B RedPajama tokens; single A100-80GB; sequences 6,144-30,720 tokens; 50 summary tokens
papers.core_mechanism: Recurrent summary vectors: document processed in segments, summary vectors of previous segments prepended as soft prompts for LM loss on the next segment (BPTT with stop-gradient after 2 steps, randomized segment lengths). Supervision is dense next-token CE on thousands of continuation tokens whose prediction requires the summary content. Base is finetuned, not frozen.
papers.measured_result: ~40x compression per segment (2048 -> 50 vectors) with sustained perplexity gains out to 28K tokens of compressed history; compressing 90 ICL demonstrations into summary vectors beats plain-text demos on several of 11 classification tasks at lower cost. RMT baseline without summary accumulation fails to use distant context.

papers.title: xRAG: Extreme Context Compression for RAG with One Token
papers.scale_tested: Mistral-7B and Mixtral-8x7B decoder FROZEN, retriever (SFR/dense embedding) FROZEN; only a 2-layer MLP projector trained (0.46% of 7B params); paraphrase pretraining on a retrieval corpus then instruction tuning; standard multi-GPU setup
papers.core_mechanism: One retrieval embedding projected into token space = 1-token document. Two-stage: (1) paraphrase pretraining — LLM must REGENERATE the document conditioned on the projected token ('The above text could be paraphrased as: [D]'), dense CE on every document token; (2) context-aware instruction tuning with SELF-DISTILLATION: KL(student-with-1-token || teacher = same frozen LLM with full document in context) + answer NLL, linear combination.
papers.measured_result: +10% average over six knowledge-intensive tasks vs no-retrieval; matches uncompressed RAG on several datasets at 3.53x FLOPs reduction; ablation: for Mistral-7B, pretraining and instruction tuning are 'of equal significance' — dropping either collapses performance; LoRA-on-same-data control rules out mere extra-tuning effects.

papers.title: 500xCompressor: Generalized Prompt Compression for LLMs
papers.scale_tested: Llama-3-8B-instruct FROZEN as decoder; encoder = same frozen LLM + LoRA (~0.3% params). Pretrain: ArXiv abstracts corpus (2.35M texts), 42k-103.8k steps @ batch 4, lr 1e-4; finetune ArxivQA (250k QA), 10k-20k steps @ batch 4, lr 5e-5, AdamW
papers.core_mechanism: Compressed tokens' per-layer KV VALUES (not input embeddings) are passed to the frozen decoder. Pretraining = teacher-forced regeneration of the original text from the KV of the compressed tokens (CE on every token); finetuning = QA conditioned on the same KV. No decoder parameters or added decoder modules — information provably lives in the compressed tokens (test set is post-cutoff, unseen).
papers.measured_result: 500 tokens -> 16/4/1 tokens (6x-480x); LLM retains 62.26-72.89% of its uncompressed-prompt QA capability; regenerates proper nouns and NUMBERS accurately; KV injection significantly beats embedding injection at high compression ratios; strictly-unseen eval kills memorization confound.

papers.title: A Silver Bullet or a Compromise for Full Attention? A Comprehensive Study of Gist Token-based Context Compression
papers.scale_tested: Llama-3-8B-class models, 3B SlimPajama tokens of compression training; multiple gist architectures (coarse/fine-grained KV, memory placement)
papers.core_mechanism: Systematic failure analysis of gist compression + two fixes: (1) fine-grained autoencoding — an auxiliary WEAK decoder with reconstruction loss on the gist tokens, kept during training; (2) segment-wise token importance estimation — upweight CE on tokens that depend on the compressed context.
papers.measured_result: Gist compression near-lossless on RAG/long-doc QA but FAILS on synthetic exact recall; three failure patterns measured: lost-by-the-boundary, lost-if-surprise (rare/unexpected tokens — i.e., numbers — dropped first when budget is tight), lost-along-the-way. Both fixes significantly improve recall; joint use best. Directly predicts that HLWM's numeric premises are the hardest content class for a latent channel without an explicit reconstruction loss.

papers.title: Say More with Less: Understanding Prompt Learning Behaviors through Gist Compression (Gist-COCO)
papers.scale_tested: FlanT5 (base-scale encoder-decoder, sub-1B) as the frozen backbone; only a plugin compression encoder finetuned; gist representations also verbalized and transferred to larger LLMs
papers.core_mechanism: Plugin encoder produces gist-token representations prepended to the frozen model's decoder inputs; trained with KL divergence between the frozen model's output distribution given RAW prompts (teacher) and given gist tokens (student) — pure distillation-from-uncompressed, no decoder updates.
papers.measured_result: Outperforms prior prompt-compression baselines on passage and instruction compression at high compression rates with a sub-1B frozen backbone — the closest existing demonstration that a frozen small model can be made to read learned prefixes via distillation alone.

papers.title: Training Large Language Models to Reason in a Continuous Latent Space (Coconut)
papers.scale_tested: GPT-2 (124M!), effective batch 128, lr 1e-4 class; GSM8k (iCoT-augmented ~385k), ProntoQA, ProsQA (~10-20k rows); single-node training
papers.core_mechanism: Last hidden state fed back as next input embedding = continuous thought. Multi-stage curriculum: stage k replaces the first k language CoT steps with c=2 latent thoughts each, CE on the REMAINING text tokens supervises the latent positions; optimizer reset at stage switches. Dense CE through the latent tokens at every stage — never asked to 'emerge'.
papers.measured_result: At 124M: GSM8k 34.1% vs No-CoT 16.5% (CoT 42.9%); ProntoQA 99.8% vs CoT 98.8%; ProsQA 97.0% vs CoT 77.5%. Ablation: WITHOUT the curriculum, accuracy collapses to 14.4/52.4/76.1 — i.e., latent channels trained end-to-end without staged dense supervision fail exactly the way HLWM's workspace failed.

papers.title: From Explicit CoT to Implicit CoT: Learning to Internalize CoT Step by Step (iCoT)
papers.scale_tested: GPT-2 Small (124M) and Medium; 9x9 multiplication (synthetic, ~800k) and GSM8k-augmented (~385k)
papers.core_mechanism: Curriculum that deletes CoT tokens from the front a few at a time while training CE on the remainder, forcing the computation into hidden states; optimizer reset per stage.
papers.measured_result: GPT-2 Small reaches ~99% on 9x9 multiplication with no explicit CoT at inference and 30% GSM8k (vs 16.5% no-CoT) — second independent demonstration that 124M models internalize multi-step content into non-textual state when supervision is dense and staged.

papers.title: Recurrent Memory Transformer (RMT)
papers.scale_tested: GPT-2-class backbones (~100-140M) on algorithmic copy/reverse/associative-retrieval and enwik8/WikiText LM; 10-20 memory tokens, BPTT across segments
papers.core_mechanism: Learned memory tokens appended per segment; their output states are the only carrier of cross-segment information; trained with plain LM/task CE via BPTT — again dense CE where the target is unpredictable without memory content.
papers.measured_result: Solves cross-segment copy/retrieval tasks near-perfectly at ~100M scale where a no-memory baseline fails; memory tokens verifiably transport content between segments. (AutoCompressors later showed RMT-style training needs summary accumulation to scale.)

papers.title: The Power of Scale for Parameter-Efficient Prompt Tuning
papers.scale_tested: T5 60M -> 11B on SuperGLUE; 1-150 soft tokens
papers.core_mechanism: Task-level soft prompts trained by gradient descent against task CE (no reconstruction; frozen base).
papers.measured_result: ADVERSARIAL DATA POINT: prompt tuning only matches full finetuning at ~10B params; at sub-1B there is a large persistent gap. Per-token capacity of soft prompts read by small frozen models is limited — do not expect 1-4 tokens to suffice at 0.6B; HLWM's 42 tokens for a ~25-token premise is the right side of this tradeoff.

papers.title: Prefix-Tuning: Optimizing Continuous Prompts for Generation
papers.scale_tested: GPT-2 Medium 355M and BART-large 400M, frozen; 0.1% trained params; table-to-text (E2E/WebNLG/DART) + summarization; standard single-GPU-era budgets
papers.core_mechanism: Trained per-LAYER key-value prefixes (activation-level, not embedding-level — same lesson as 500xCompressor's KV finding) with task CE; reparameterized through an MLP for optimization stability.
papers.measured_result: Matches full finetuning on table-to-text at 355M frozen base — canonical proof that sub-1B frozen decoders CAN be steered through learned KV prefixes when the objective is dense generation CE; embedding-only prefixes were notably less stable/effective.

lenses.recipe: DIAGNOSIS FROM THE LITERATURE: every system that gets content through a latent prefix into a (usually frozen) decoder shares ONE ingredient HLWM never had: a dense, token-level CE/KL objective THROUGH the prefix whose targets are unpredictable without the prefix content — reconstruction/regeneration (ICAE, 500xCompressor, xRAG paraphrase stage, fine-grained AE in 2412.17483), distillation to the same model given the uncompressed text (xRAG self-KD, Gist-COCO), or masked instruction CE with full finetuning (gisting) or curriculum (Coconut/iCoT). HLWM v6-v9 had structural necessity (masking) but only sparse supervision: a few answer tokens the model could satisfy by abstaining, plus a w=0.1 probe. Masking is necessary but not sufficient; reconstruction is the missing half. Second lesson: HLWM's KL-to-base anchor was distillation to the WRONG teacher (base WITHOUT the premise = directed pressure to ignore the prefix); xRAG/Gist-COCO distill to the base WITH the raw text — flip the reference. Third: 500x/prefix-tuning show per-layer KV injection beats input-embedding injection for frozen decoders. V10 CHANNEL RECIPE: (0) Architecture: keep encoder = frozen base + LoRA r16 (validated config of ICAE/500x); prefix 42-64 tokens for a ≤25-token premise + gold trace (compression ratio <2x, far inside ICAE's near-lossless 4x regime); DELETE all scalar gates and zero-init on the read-out path — ICAE/500x use standard init; readability comes from the objective (and v6-v9 proved zero-init structures stay dead). Prefer injecting the prefix as per-layer KV (500xCompressor, prefix-tuning); if plumbing risk on Qwen3-GQA/T4 is too high, embedding injection is acceptable at our low ratio but must pass the reconstruction gate below. (1) STAGE 1 — reconstruction pretraining, ~40% of steps (~1300 of 3200), lr 1e-4 AdamW (ICAE/500x values): decoder conditioned ONLY on [prefix; task-token [AE]] teacher-forced to regenerate premise + gold reasoning trace, CE weight 1.0 on every token (~60-100 CE terms/row vs v9's ~5). Rows are free (synthetic): generate 30-50k distinct (premise, trace) pairs for this stage; sequences are short, so grad-accum can rise to 8-16 at constant wall-clock. HARD GATE at stage end: held-out premise reconstruction BLEU ≥0.95 AND digit-level exact-match ≥0.98 (numbers are the 'lost-if-surprise' class per 2412.17483 — gate on digits, not BLEU alone). If this gate fails, the channel is dead for structural reasons and stage 2 is not run. (2) STAGE 2 — task + distillation, remaining ~1900 steps, lr 5e-5, optimizer state reset at the switch (Coconut/iCoT both reset): total loss = 1.0 * masked-row answer CE + 0.5 * continued reconstruction CE (kept alive per fine-grained-AE finding to prevent drift) + 1.0 * token-level KL(decoder-with-prefix || same frozen base given raw premise in context) computed on answer tokens (xRAG's self-distillation, teacher has the text, student has only the prefix; temperature 1). Ban the old KL-to-base-no-context entirely. (3) Structural necessity on EVERY row: keep v9's physical premise withholding on masked rows, and apply a gisting-style attention mask on unmasked rows (post-prefix tokens cannot attend premise tokens) so 100% of rows train the channel instead of ~30%. (4) Optional curriculum if trace-following is wanted: stage the trace out Coconut-style (keep first k trace steps as text, replace earlier steps with latent, 2-3 stages) rather than asking the prefix to carry the whole computation at once; w/o-curriculum ablation in Coconut collapsed 34.1->14.4, which is the HLWM failure signature. (5) LANES under this lens: give each lane a DIFFERENT reconstruction target (lane 1: premise entities/units; lane 2: constraints/comparisons; lane 3: gold-trace step k) — per-lane dense AE loss makes cosine-0.95 collapse impossible unless the targets are identical, replacing the 9x-failed diversity penalties with supervision. (6) EXPERTS: same principle — per-expert reconstruction/target specialization by family, assigned (not learned-routed) at train time; learned routing only as a later, separately-gated add-on, since no paper in this lens shows emergent routing at this scale. (7) Diagnostics each 512 steps: held-out reconstruction BLEU/digit-EM, masked-vs-unmasked accuracy gap, mean per-token KL to the with-context teacher; abort criteria preregistered on the stage-1 gate.
lenses.feasibility_at_our_budget: Partially supported, with one honest gap. FOR: (a) the frozen-decoder + LoRA-encoder configuration is exactly the validated one — ICAE, 500xCompressor, xRAG, and Gist-COCO all keep the decoder frozen and still achieve near-perfect content transport, so HLWM's frozen 0.6B base is not the blocker; (b) capacity is over-provisioned: ICAE gets ~100% BLEU/EM reconstructing 300-token arbitrary Pile text into 128 slots on a 7B; we need ~25-token templated premises from 4 synthetic families into 42 tokens (ratio <2x vs their 4x), a task orders of magnitude lower-entropy; (c) sub-1B existence proofs exist for the core mechanism (dense CE through latent tokens): Coconut and iCoT at GPT-2 124M solve multi-step synthetic reasoning through latent state, RMT transports content through 10-20 memory tokens at ~100M, prefix-tuning steers a frozen 355M through KV prefixes, Gist-COCO reads learned prefixes into a frozen sub-1B FlanT5; (d) 500xCompressor's optimizer regime (batch 4, AdamW, lr 1e-4/5e-5) is literally our regime. AGAINST: (e) data/step volume — the compression papers use 1.7e5-5e7 training sequences vs our ~12.8-25k gradient rows; this is offset by the tiny content entropy but is NOT directly evidenced at 7.5-50k rows, so the stage-1 reconstruction gate is the honest kill-switch (if 42 tokens can't learn to regenerate 25-token templated premises in 1300 steps, nothing downstream was ever going to work); (f) the Lester scale result warns soft-prompt information per token is lower at 0.6B — mitigated by 42-64 tokens and KV injection, not solved; (g) stage-2 transfer (reconstruction -> masked-task use) in ~1900 steps is the genuinely under-evidenced step; xRAG's ablation says both stages matter equally, and our stage 2 is thin. Net: reconstruction readability at our budget is a defensible bet with a cheap early gate; full task-transfer parity is a stretch and should be preregistered as a directional claim (masked-row accuracy >> 0 and > shuffled-prefix control), not parity with the text-in-context ceiling. Lanes-via-distinct-reconstruction-targets is low-risk (pure dense supervision). Emergent expert routing remains unsupported by this literature at any scale we can afford.
risks: Scale gap on the headline systems: ICAE/500x/xRAG results are at 7-8B with 1.7e5-5e7 training sequences; no paper demonstrates prompt-compression reconstruction at 0.6B with <50k rows — the stage-1 digit-EM gate must be allowed to kill the mechanism early.

Numbers are the first content lost: 2412.17483's 'lost-if-surprise' failure pattern means numeric premise tokens are precisely the hardest class; gating on BLEU alone would pass a channel that drops digits — gate on digit-level exact match.

Stage-2 interference: adding task CE + KL can erode reconstruction (drift back to posterior collapse); the fine-grained-AE finding says keep the reconstruction loss on at 0.5 weight, but the interaction at 1900 steps is untested.

Distillation teacher ceiling: the with-context teacher is the same 0.6B base, whose own accuracy on these families bounds what KL can transfer; if base-with-premise accuracy is low on hard bands, the KL term supervises toward a weak target (measure teacher accuracy per band first).

KV-injection engineering risk: per-layer KV plumbing into Qwen3 GQA on T4/bf16 is nontrivial and 500x's KV-vs-embedding advantage was measured at 30-480x compression; at our <2x ratio embedding injection may suffice — do not spend budget on KV unless the embedding-level stage-1 gate fails.

Decoder-side LoRA can cheat: unlike ICAE's strictly frozen decoder, HLWM trains LoRA in the decoder too; on any row where the premise is visible the LoRA can bypass the prefix — the gisting attention mask must cover ALL rows or the channel trains on a minority slice again.

lenses.lens: MoE routing collapse and small-expert-count fixes (aux losses, z-loss, hash/structural routing, expert-choice, DeepSeekMoE shared experts, SoftMoE/Lory/SMEAR differentiable routing, BASE assignment, StableMoE distillation, batch-size-1 LBL statistics)

papers.title: Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models with Simple and Efficient Sparsity
papers.scale_tested: 223M-1.6T params, C4 pretraining (hundreds of B tokens), TPU pods; nothing near 7.5k rows
papers.core_mechanism: Top-1 token routing + auxiliary load-balance loss L=alpha*N*sum(f_i*P_i), alpha=0.01; capacity factor >1 buffers imbalance
papers.measured_result: alpha=1e-2 sufficient for balance without hurting CE; <1% dropped tokens needed for scaling; loss->1 at perfect balance. No collapse guarantee — it is a soft pressure, and HLWM already saw it fail to bind when most emissions were invalid

papers.title: ST-MoE: Designing Stable and Transferable Sparse Expert Models
papers.scale_tested: FLOP-matched to T5-XL (~4B eq.), 32 experts, mC4 multilingual pretraining
papers.core_mechanism: Router z-loss L_RZ=(1/B)*sum(logsumexp(logits)^2), weight 1e-3, penalizes large router logits (bf16 roundoff is the instability source)
papers.measured_result: Stabilized training with no quality loss where LR clamps/grad clipping cost quality; adopted at beta=0.001 by OLMoE and others. Stability fix, not a collapse fix — orthogonal, cheap, directly relevant to your bf16 T4 runs

papers.title: Hash Layers For Large Sparse Models
papers.scale_tested: ~750M-4.5B dense-equivalent Transformers, pushshift/RoBERTa-era LM + dialogue corpora
papers.core_mechanism: Fixed random/balanced hash of the token id -> expert; zero routing parameters, zero balance loss, collapse impossible by construction
papers.measured_result: Matches or beats Switch and BASE on LM perplexity; balanced random hashes on LOCAL features beat learned clustering. Direct evidence that at small expert counts LEARNED routing buys ~nothing over deterministic assignment

papers.title: Mixture-of-Experts with Expert Choice Routing
papers.scale_tested: 100M-8B activated params, GLaM-style pretraining corpus, 64-128 experts, large TPU batches
papers.core_mechanism: Experts pick top-k tokens (fixed bucket per expert) -> perfect load balance by construction, no aux loss
papers.measured_result: ~2x pretraining convergence speedup vs Switch/GShard top-2. CRITICAL CAVEAT for you: selection uses batch/sequence statistics — at batch size 1 autoregressive decoding it is causally invalid and degenerate (train/test mismatch); their own appendix shows hash routing worse only in their large-batch regime

papers.title: BASE Layers: Simplifying Training of Large, Sparse Models
papers.scale_tested: 1.5B+ LMs, large distributed batches (assignment solved over thousands of tokens/worker)
papers.core_mechanism: Token-expert allocation as linear assignment (truncated Bertsekas auction) -> exactly equal tokens per expert, no aux loss or new hyperparameters
papers.measured_result: Matched/beat Switch with guaranteed balance; Clark et al. 2022 found significant runtime overhead, replaced with Sinkhorn + capacity 2. Balance guaranteed only within the assignment batch — meaningless at batch 1

papers.title: DeepSeekMoE: Towards Ultimate Expert Specialization
papers.scale_tested: 2B (validation scale, single GPU, 100B tokens, 25k steps) and 16B/145B
papers.core_mechanism: Fine-grained expert segmentation + K_s SHARED always-on experts isolating common knowledge so routed experts must specialize; expert-level balance loss
papers.measured_result: At 2B single-device: expert balance factor alpha=0.01 prevented routing collapse (0.001 at 16B); DeepSeekMoE 2B ~ GShard 2.9B with 1.5x expert params; shared:activated 1:3 ratio robust (Pile loss 1.808/1.806/1.811 for 1/2/4 shared). The shared-expert isolation is the published fix for exactly your v5.6.2 finding that 'experts carried content'

papers.title: From Sparse to Soft Mixtures of Experts (SoftMoE)
papers.scale_tested: ViT-S/16 to ViT-H, JFT-4B image pretraining; encoder-only
papers.core_mechanism: Each expert processes p learned SLOTS = softmax-weighted convex combinations of all tokens; fully differentiable, no discrete routing, no balance loss, collapse impossible
papers.measured_result: Beat sparse MoE and dense ViTs at matched inference cost. CAVEAT: slots mix tokens across positions -> breaks autoregressive causality; not directly usable in your decoder without Lory-style segment tricks; evidence is vision-only

papers.title: Lory: Fully Differentiable MoE for Autoregressive LM Pre-training
papers.scale_tested: 0.3B/1.5B active params, 150B tokens pretraining
papers.core_mechanism: SMEAR-style expert parameter MERGING (softmax-weighted average of expert weights) made causal via segment-level routing (route segment t+1 with segment t's representation) + similarity-based batching to induce specialization
papers.measured_result: Beat dense equal-FLOP baselines (+perplexity and downstream) with NO load-balancing objective; experts specialize at DOMAIN level only when similar docs are batched together — random batching killed specialization. Segment routing is the published causal fix for merging in decoders

papers.title: Soft Merging of Experts with Adaptive Routing (SMEAR)
papers.scale_tested: T5-Base/T5-GLUE multitask FINE-TUNING (8 GLUE tasks) and ResNet-DomainNet — the closest published setting to HLWM's scale
papers.core_mechanism: Compute merged expert = router-probability-weighted average of expert PARAMETERS; fully differentiable; router gets exact gradients (their diagnosis: discrete-routing gradient ESTIMATORS are why learned routing underperforms heuristics)
papers.measured_result: GLUE avg 81.6+-1.0: beats ALL gradient estimators (REINFORCE, ST) and heuristic tag routing (+2.7% T5-GLUE), beats parameter-matched single expert +1.4%; experts show task-level specialization; throughput ~= top-1 routing. Replicated small-scale evidence that differentiable merging avoids collapse where learned discrete routing fails

papers.title: DEMix Layers: Disentangling Domains for Modular Language Modeling
papers.scale_tested: 125M-1.3B autoregressive LMs, 8 domains, ~100B tokens total but per-domain experts trained on domain shards
papers.core_mechanism: DETERMINISTIC routing by known domain label (document provenance); no router, no balance loss; parameter-free posterior-weighted ensemble of experts at inference for unseen domains
papers.measured_result: Lower test perplexity than dense AND than learned top-1 MoE at matched compute; experts addable/removable post-hoc. Canonical proof that when labels exist (your synthetic families), metadata routing works where learned routing collapses

papers.title: StableMoE: Stable Routing Strategy for Mixture of Experts
papers.scale_tested: Base/Large LM configs (~450M class) on LM + multilingual MT; standard academic budgets
papers.core_mechanism: Stage 1: learn balanced routing and DISTILL it (L_task+L_bal+L_dis) into a lightweight decoupled router (word embedding router suffices); Stage 2: FREEZE the distilled router, train experts with L_task only — eliminates routing fluctuation
papers.measured_result: Beat Switch/BASE/Hash in convergence speed and final perplexity in both base and large settings; frozen-router stage has zero routing fluctuation by construction. This is the published template for 'structural routing first, learned router distilled afterwards'

papers.title: Demons in the Detail: Implementing Load Balancing Loss for Specialized MoE (+ Loss-Free Balancing, 2408.15664)
papers.scale_tested: 3.4B-scale MoE LLMs (Qwen team), 100B+ tokens; ablations over balance-batch-size
papers.core_mechanism: THE batch-size-1 answer: micro-batch LBL (f_i computed per micro-batch, i.e., per sequence at bsz 1) forces uniform routing WITHIN each sequence -> provably inhibits domain/family specialization; fix = accumulate expert-selection counts f_i across micro-batches/accum steps into a global-batch LBL (extra stat-sync only)
papers.measured_result: Global-batch LBL beat micro-batch LBL in ALL settings; with micro-batch balance, domain-specific sequences showed NO expert selection differences (specialization erased); with global-batch, clear domain specialization emerged; micro-batch also degraded DeepSeek's loss-free bias method (u=0.001 additive-sign bias, arXiv:2408.15664, validated to 3B/200B tokens) — that method's running-count bias is itself inherently global-batch and gradient-interference-free

lenses.recipe: RANKED STRATEGIES FOR N=2-3 EXPERTS AT HLWM SCALE.
