(1st — use as primary) STRUCTURAL ROUTING BY TASK FAMILY + STABLEMOE DISTILLATION: you have gold family labels on 100% of rows (synthetic data), which is exactly the DEMix/Task-MoE precondition. Architecture: 2 routed LoRA experts + 1 always-on SHARED LoRA expert (DeepSeekMoE isolation — the shared expert absorbs the common content your v5.6.2 ablation showed the experts were hoarding, so a routed expert's removal no longer guts probe content). Sequence-level routing (Task-MoE showed sequence/task routing beats token routing for deployability; token-level routing at 0.6B/7.5k rows has no evidence). Family->expert map fixed a priori (e.g., {numeric, unit}->E1, {ordering, abstention}->E2), stratified sampling so each grad-accum window of 4 contains balanced families — load balance is then a property of the DATALOADER, not a loss; collapse is impossible by construction (Hash Layers proves deterministic assignment costs ~nothing vs learned routing at small N). Steps 0-2600: hard one-hot routing from the label; NO balance loss, NO router gradient into experts; add router as a detached linear probe on mean-pooled prompt hidden state trained with CE-to-family-label, weight 0.1 (StableMoE Stage-1 distillation, L_dis only since balance comes free). Steps 2600-3200 (StableMoE Stage 2): switch routing source to the FROZEN argmax of the distilled router; gates: held-out router family-accuracy >=0.95; end-task delta between label-routed and router-routed <=0.02; causal specialization test = cross-routing ablation (send family-A rows through E2) must cost >=0.05 accuracy, else 'experts' are redundant and the section goes negative-evidence. (2nd — differentiable comparison arm, cheap for LoRA) SMEAR/LORY MERGING: because experts are LoRA deltas, the merged expert is just deltaW = sum_i p_i * (B_i A_i) — compute the weighted sum of the ΔW products (NOT of A and B separately), one router softmax per sequence over the pooled PROMPT representation (prompt-only pooling preserves causality, Lory's segment trick degenerates to this at your 1-routing-decision-per-row granularity). No balance loss needed (SMEAR used none); add ST-MoE z-loss 1e-3 on router logits for bf16 safety; optionally add DEMix-style light CE-to-family on the router (weight 0.05) since Lory showed specialization needs a batching/label prior, which your stratified sampler provides. SMEAR's T5-GLUE numbers (beats REINFORCE/ST estimators AND tag routing, +1.4% over param-matched single expert) are the only replicated fine-tuning-scale evidence in this whole literature — this arm is the honest 'can routing be learned here at all' test. (3rd — do NOT use as primary) LEARNED TOP-1 + AUX LOSSES DONE RIGHT: if any learned discrete routing is retained, (a) NEVER compute LBL per micro-batch — at batch 1 it is a per-sequence uniformity constraint that actively erases family specialization (Demons in the Detail, measured); accumulate f_i counts in a buffer across >=64 sequences (all grad-accum steps + a running window) before computing L=alpha*N*sum(f_i*P_i), alpha=0.01 (DeepSeekMoE's validated single-device value); (b) or use DeepSeek loss-free bias, additive sign update u=0.001 on running loads (no interference gradients — relevant given your inert-penalty history); (c) z-loss 1e-3; (d) no zero-init anywhere on the router path (your RMSNorm-inertness finding; SMEAR/Switch both use small-normal router init). Expert-choice and BASE are ELIMINATED for v10: both derive their balance guarantee from batch statistics that do not exist at batch 1, and EC token-selection is causally invalid at autoregressive inference. Budget: strategy 1 adds ~0 FLOPs over v9 (routing is an index); strategy 2 adds one weighted sum of 2-3 LoRA ΔWs per row (~negligible at r16). Both fit in the 6.5h envelope with the 3200-step schedule unchanged.
lenses.feasibility_at_our_budget: STRONG for strategy 1, MODERATE for strategy 2, WEAK for learned discrete routing. Balanced specialization with N=2-3 experts is essentially guaranteed under label routing — DEMix demonstrated it at 125M-1.3B autoregressive LMs, Task-MoE at sequence granularity, Hash Layers showed learned routing adds nothing over deterministic assignment, and MoV/MoLoRA (arXiv:2309.05444) demonstrated LoRA-expert mixtures beating plain LoRA at 770M with <=3.2% trainable params — all consistent with 0.6B frozen-base+LoRA. SMEAR is the single closest match to your regime (T5-Base multitask fine-tuning, ~10k-row-scale GLUE tasks) and worked there, so the differentiable arm is plausible but single-paper at that scale. Two honest caveats: (i) with 7.5k rows split 2-3 ways, each routed expert sees ~2.5-4k rows — the shared expert is what keeps this from starving; consider 25-50k rows since gold traces are free; (ii) the literature guarantees balance and family-specialization, NOT that 2 specialized r16 experts beat one r32 monolithic LoRA at matched trainable params — no paper at this scale runs that exact control, and HLWM's own plain-LoRA control is still unrun after 10 studies. The distilled-router step is near-certain to pass (family is lexically recoverable from synthetic prompts) — which also means router accuracy alone is a weak scientific claim; the cross-routing causal ablation is the load-bearing gate.
risks: Micro-batch LBL trap: at batch 1 x accum 4, any balance loss computed per forward is a PER-SEQUENCE uniformity penalty that measurably erases specialization (arXiv:2501.11873) — v10 must accumulate routing stats across a >=64-sequence buffer or use no balance loss at all

Specialization without benefit: no paper at this scale shows N=2 label-routed experts beating a matched-capacity single LoRA; the cross-routing ablation and the (still unrun) plain-LoRA control can both come back null, converting the expert section to negative evidence a 4th time

Router distillation is trivially easy on synthetic data (family is surface-recoverable), so a passing router-accuracy gate certifies the DATA, not the mechanism — claim must be scoped to 'structural routing + recovered router', not 'learned routing works'

Expert data starvation: 7.5k rows / 2-3 experts ~ 2.5-4k rows per routed expert; DeepSeekMoE-style shared expert mitigates but DEMix-style per-domain quality at <5k rows/expert is untested in the literature

SMEAR arm subtlety: merging LoRA factors A_i,B_i separately is NOT the weighted mixture of ΔW_i=B_iA_i (nonlinearity of the product); must merge the ΔW products or the differentiable arm silently tests a different model

Sequence-level routing means the routing decision is made from the prompt only; if family cues concentrate late in the prompt, pooled-prompt router and mid-training distillation may disagree with the label map on held-out phrasings — gate router accuracy on paraphrase-shifted rows, not just canonical templates

lenses.lens: Preventing representation collapse between parallel streams/heads/ensemble members (decorrelation losses that bite, head-disagreement regularization, DPP/NCL diversity, structural asymmetry, hard-assignment specialization)

papers.title: Multi-Head Attention with Disagreement Regularization
papers.scale_tested: Transformer-Base ~65M and Big ~210M, WMT17 Zh-En (20M pairs) + WMT14 En-De (4M pairs), standard single-run NMT training
papers.core_mechanism: Auxiliary loss = mean pairwise cosine similarity of raw head OUTPUT vectors (also subspace-value and attended-position variants), added to likelihood with lambda=1.0, no new parameters, penalty applied per-example directly on the activations (no batch statistics needed)
papers.measured_result: Output-disagreement drove measured head disagreement exp(D) from 0.881 to 0.997 (near-orthogonal outputs); +0.65 BLEU Zh-En / +0.87 BLEU En-De at Base (27.64->28.51, p<0.01); combining the 3 terms did NOT stack (24.78 single vs 24.60 all three); 12% train-speed cost when applied to all attention nets

papers.title: Reducing Overfitting in Deep Networks by Decorrelating Representations (DeCov)
papers.scale_tested: MNIST/CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100/ImageNet AlexNet-scale CNNs (<=60M params), standard single-GPU-era budgets
papers.core_mechanism: Penalize squared off-diagonal entries of the minibatch cross-covariance of hidden activations (diagonal/variance exempt), as a plug-in regularizer on any layer
papers.measured_result: Always reduced train-val gap, usually matched/beat Dropout on val accuracy; later work documents the failure mode directly relevant to us: covariance estimate is singular/garbage when minibatch << feature dim (our batch is 1)

papers.title: VICReg: Variance-Invariance-Covariance Regularization
papers.scale_tested: ResNet-50 on ImageNet (large), but the loss is architecture-agnostic and widely replicated on CIFAR-scale encoders; coefficients 25/25/1 (inv/var/cov), 8192-dim expander
papers.core_mechanism: Hinge variance term mean(relu(1 - std(z_dim))) per dimension + off-diagonal covariance penalty; the VARIANCE HINGE is the canonical live-gradient scale-invariance breaker (a norm-invariant cosine or gated penalty cannot be cheated to zero because std must exceed 1)
papers.measured_result: 73.2% ImageNet linear-probe top-1, on par with SOTA joint-embedding methods, with explicit (not architectural) collapse prevention; ablations show removing the variance term collapses training

papers.title: Stochastic Multiple Choice Learning for Training Diverse Deep Ensembles
papers.scale_tested: CIFAR-10 CNN ensembles, FCN semantic segmentation, CNN+RNN captioning; 4-6 members, standard 2016 single-GPU budgets
papers.core_mechanism: Winner-take-all oracle loss: each example's gradient goes ONLY to the lowest-error member; specialization emerges from exclusive hard assignment, not from any diversity penalty
papers.measured_result: Lower oracle error than independent ensembles and classical MCL across all 3 task types, 5x faster than MCL; members visibly specialize by class/subset; follow-up CMCL (arXiv:1706.03475) got 14.05%/6.60% relative top-1 error reduction on CIFAR/SVHN with 5 ResNets

papers.title: DVERGE: Diversifying Vulnerabilities for Enhanced Robust Generation of Ensembles
papers.scale_tested: Ensembles of 3/5/8 ResNet-20s (~0.27M each) on CIFAR-10, round-robin training, adversarial-training-comparable compute
papers.core_mechanism: Round-robin distillation of each member's non-robust features into inputs the OTHER members must classify correctly - i.e., decorrelate error surfaces via each other's failure cases rather than via a geometric penalty
papers.measured_result: Inter-member transfer-attack success rate dropped from >60% (prior ensemble diversity methods incl. ADP/GAL) to <6%; robustness grows with member count - strongest evidence that functional/error diversity, not representation geometry, is what soft cosine penalties fail to deliver

papers.title: Pathologies of Predictive Diversity in Deep Ensembles
papers.scale_tested: 231 controlled experiments: small CNNs vs WideResNet-scale members on CIFAR-10/100 class ensembles
papers.core_mechanism: Systematically add diversity-encouraging and diversity-discouraging terms to ensemble training and measure ensemble loss vs member capacity
papers.measured_result: For SMALL-capacity members (our regime), discouraging diversity hurt in 56% of 82 experiments and helped in only 4%; for large members, 74% of 149 experiments were same-or-better WITHOUT diversity - diversity losses pay off precisely at small member capacity

papers.title: A Unified Theory of Diversity in Ensemble Learning
papers.scale_tested: Theory (exact bias-variance-diversity decompositions for squared/CE/Poisson losses) + small tabular/vision demonstrations
papers.core_mechanism: Diversity is a third term in an exact loss decomposition, statistically dependent on bias and variance - it cannot be maximized freely; enforced diversity is paid for in member fit
papers.measured_result: Proves diversity-maximization objectives trade directly against member bias; explains GNCL (arXiv:2011.02952) finding that NCL penalty strength must shrink as member capacity grows

papers.title: Repulsive Deep Ensembles are Bayesian
papers.scale_tested: MLPs/small CNNs, 1D regression + UCI + CIFAR, particle ensembles of ~10 members
papers.core_mechanism: Kernelized repulsion term between members in weight space or function space (SVGD/Wasserstein gradient flow); function-space repulsion evaluated on training inputs
papers.measured_result: Function-space repulsion recovers HMC-like epistemic uncertainty where weight-space repulsion fails (different weights can be the same function - directly explains why our structurally asymmetric tensor_split inputs still collapsed); BUT follow-ups (arXiv:2306.02775) report NO significant accuracy gains over vanilla ensembles on real tasks - repulsion buys distinctness, not accuracy

papers.title: How Does SimSiam Avoid Collapse Without Negative Samples?
papers.scale_tested: ResNet-18/50 on CIFAR-10/ImageNet-100/ImageNet; standard SSL budgets, mechanism verified in small ablations
papers.core_mechanism: Collapse is prevented by ARCHITECTURAL ASYMMETRY (predictor MLP on exactly one path, optimized toward the other path's stop-gradient output); the asymmetric extra gradient provides de-centering + dimensional de-correlation
papers.measured_result: Removing stop-gradient diverges; a SYMMETRIC predictor still collapses - asymmetric inputs alone (our tensor_split) are the weakest form of asymmetry and are not what the mechanism requires; the asymmetry must be in the computational path/objective

papers.title: Convergent World Representations and Divergent Tasks
papers.scale_tested: Multi-task fine-tuning of small/mid transformers across 2-3 tasks, CKA layer-wise analysis
papers.core_mechanism: Measures CKA between representations of models/streams trained on different supervised tasks over shared inputs
papers.measured_result: CKA saturates ~0.85 in mid layers for 2-3 task training, and models trained on COMPLETELY DISJOINT task pairs still show substantially elevated alignment; arXiv:2505.13899 shows task overlap drives alignment independent of data overlap - DIRECT evidence that per-stream task supervision alone does NOT keep streams representationally distinct

papers.title: Mixture-of-Depths: Dynamically allocating compute in transformer-based language models
papers.scale_tested: isoFLOP LM pretraining sweeps (tens of M to ~1B+ params, DeepMind compute - far above our budget)
papers.core_mechanism: Hard top-k capacity constraint (e.g., 12.5% of tokens pass through a block) forces the router to specialize token allocation; specialization arises from enforced SCARCITY, not a diversity penalty
papers.measured_result: Matches/beats isoFLOP baselines with up to ~50% fewer FLOPs per forward pass; consistent with sMCL/MoD theme: hard structural constraints induce specialization where soft penalties fail - but only tested at LM-pretraining scale, treat as design principle not recipe

papers.title: Orthogonality Constrained Multi-Head Attention for Keyword Spotting
papers.scale_tested: Small keyword-spotting models (<1M params), single-GPU
papers.core_mechanism: Frobenius penalties on inter-head Gram matrices of context/score vectors (inter-head non-orthogonality) plus intra-head consistency term
papers.measured_result: Measured inter-head orthogonality increases through training with accuracy improvement on KWS - replicates Li et al.'s 'penalty on raw outputs bites' at sub-1M scale

lenses.recipe: V10 two-lane recipe - ship all five pieces together; each alone has a documented failure mode. (1) PER-LANE DENSE SUPERVISION with disjoint targets from gold traces: lane1 head = token-level CE reconstructing the premise (gold available for every synthetic row); lane2 head = CE over the operator/step sequence. Weight 1.0 each, computed on every row. This keeps both lanes alive and information-bounded but per the CKA literature will NOT alone prevent cosine ~0.9 convergence. (2) OUTPUT DISAGREEMENT PENALTY (the workhorse, per-example so it works at batch 1 x accum 4): L_dis = mean over prefix-token positions of cos(h1_t, h2_t) on the RAW pre-RMSNorm lane outputs, lambda = 1.0 exactly (Li et al.'s value; typical 0.01-0.1 'penalty hygiene' weights are why such terms read as inert). Ship a step-0 unit test asserting grad-norm of L_dis w.r.t. lane parameters > 1e-6 (kills the inert-penalty recurrence class); no zero-init scalar gate anywhere upstream of this loss - the gate zeroed the gradient twice already. (3) SCALE-INVARIANCE BREAKER + CROSS-DECORRELATION over the TOKEN axis, not the batch axis (batch 1 makes batch covariance rank-1 garbage, the documented DeCov failure): per lane, VICReg hinge L_var = mean_d relu(1 - std_tokens(h_l)) with weight 1.0; cross-lane L_xcov = ||Corr_tokens(h1, h2)||_F^2 / d with weight 1.0, where Corr uses token-axis standardization (16+ prefix tokens per lane per row; optionally EMA the correlation across accum steps). The hinge is what makes the penalty live under RMSNorm scale invariance. (4) ARCHITECTURAL ASYMMETRY, not input asymmetry: give lane2 (only) a 2-layer predictor MLP trained to predict stop-grad(h1)'s task features, or at minimum make lane head depths/objectives structurally different - Zhang et al. show symmetric paths collapse even with stop-gradient, and tensor_split input asymmetry is exactly the kind that does not count. (5) HARD-ASSIGNMENT OPTION for any loss the lanes share (e.g., contribution to the downstream consumer): winner-take-all gradient routing per example (sMCL), which manufactures specialization via data partition at zero extra compute. SCHEDULE: all diversity terms ON from step 0 at full weight (Li et al. use constant lambda from scratch); if per-lane task CE stalls >20% above its solo-run reference, anneal lambda_dis 1.0 -> 0.3 over the last 40% of the 3200 steps (Pathologies trade-off). AUDIT GATES: (a) mean per-sample cosine(h1,h2) < 0.5 AND linear CKA < 0.7 (report both - CKA can stay high while cosine drops); (b) cross-lane leakage probe: post-hoc linear probe predicting lane2's target from lane1's representation must be < solo-probe-accuracy - 0.15 (geometric orthogonality does not imply informational separation); (c) necessity: lane-ablation AND lane-swap each degrade downstream graded accuracy by a preregistered margin - distinctness without necessity is the repulsive-ensembles negative result. COMPUTE: all added losses are O(tokens x d^2) on 16-43-token summaries, <2% step-time (Li et al. measured 12% applying to every attention layer of a full transformer; we touch 2 lanes once per row) - fits inside the 6.5h envelope with margin.
lenses.feasibility_at_our_budget: FEASIBLE, with the strongest evidence base of the three failed components. The core method (output-cosine disagreement at lambda=1.0 on raw activations) is proven at 65M-210M transformers on single-run NMT budgets, and again at <1M params (KWS) - at or below our 132M-trainable scale; it needs no batch statistics so batch 1 x accum 4 is fine, and the compute overhead is negligible against 6.5 GPU-h. The Pathologies result says small-capacity members are exactly the regime where diversity encouragement helps rather than hurts. The two prior HLWM failures are both explained by the literature rather than contradicting it: (i) the inert penalty was a broken instrument (zero-init gate + RMSNorm scale invariance zeroed the gradient - VICReg's variance hinge and the step-0 grad-norm test are the standard fixes), and (ii) tensor_split input asymmetry is the weakest asymmetry form, which the SimSiam analysis shows does not prevent collapse, while path/objective asymmetry does. Two honest caveats: nobody has published this exact configuration (2 latent lanes with disjoint dense targets inside a frozen-base LoRA sidecar), so this is transfer of mechanism, not replication of a system; and the literature only guarantees you can make lanes GEOMETRICALLY distinct and individually supervised - it explicitly does NOT guarantee the downstream consumer benefits (repulsive-ensembles follow-ups found no accuracy gains from distinctness alone). Preregister the claim as 'lanes distinct AND each causally necessary,' not 'diversity improves accuracy.'
risks: Per-stream supervision alone is NOT sufficient - CKA convergence occurs even across disjoint tasks (arXiv:2602.00533, 2505.13899); two near-identical vectors can co-encode both premise and operator targets and satisfy both heads. If v10 ships only per-lane targets without the disagreement+hinge terms, expect cosine collapse #10.

Batch-axis statistics are garbage at batch 1: any DeCov/VICReg-style covariance computed across the batch is rank-1; must be computed across the token axis (or EMA'd), else the loss silently optimizes noise.

Geometric decorrelation != informational decorrelation: lanes can reach cosine ~0 while encoding identical content in rotated bases; only the cross-lane leakage probe gate detects this, and no paper in this literature runs that probe - it is our addition, so it may fail in ways the literature cannot predict.

Diversity-accuracy trade (arXiv:2301.03962, 2302.00704): lambda=1.0 may tax per-lane task accuracy; mitigated by small member capacity being the favorable regime, but monitor per-lane CE against solo-run references and anneal if >20% worse.

Trivial-satisfaction cheat: a lane can satisfy the cosine penalty with a constant orthogonal direction (dead-but-orthogonal lane); the variance hinge + dense per-lane CE are the guards - shipping the penalty without both re-opens this hole.

Distinct lanes may still be ignored downstream (the repulsive-ensembles negative result: distinctness bought no task accuracy); if the lane-necessity ablation gate fails while distinctness gates pass, that is a consumer-side failure and must not be reported as a lanes success.

lenses.lens: SMALL-SCALE EMPIRICAL REALITY CHECK: what actually worked at <=1B params / <=100k rows for latent reasoning, learned routing, and prefix content-transfer (arxiv.org/abs/<id> for every entry)

papers.title: Training LLMs to Reason in a Continuous Latent Space (Coconut)
papers.scale_tested: GPT-2 124M FULL fine-tune, lr 1e-4, eff. batch 128; data: GSM8k-Aug 385,620 rows, ProntoQA 9,000 rows, ProsQA 17,886 rows; staged curriculum ~25-50 epochs (multi-day A100, GPU-h not stated)
papers.core_mechanism: Last hidden state fed back as next input embedding ('continuous thought'); staged curriculum replaces first k gold CoT steps with k*c latents per stage (optimizer reset each stage); answer CE is the only loss — latents supervised indirectly via the curriculum
papers.measured_result: GSM8K 34.1±1.5 vs CoT 42.9 / No-CoT 16.5 (loses to explicit CoT); WITHOUT curriculum 14.4 — below No-CoT; ProntoQA (9k rows) 99.8 vs CoT 98.8; ProsQA (17.9k rows) 97.0 vs CoT 77.5 — the wins are on SYNTHETIC rule-based data in our row regime, but with ~50 epochs

papers.title: From Explicit CoT to Implicit CoT: Stepwise Internalization (iCoT)
papers.scale_tested: GPT-2 Small 124M full FT (lr 5e-5, remove 4-8 CoT tokens/epoch, 50-100 epochs); also Mistral-7B; GSM8k-Aug 385k rows and synthetic multiplication data
papers.core_mechanism: Start from an explicit-CoT model, delete CoT tokens a few per epoch until none remain; the removed computation is forced into hidden states; dense gold traces required as scaffolding
papers.measured_result: GPT-2 Small: 9x9 multiplication 99% vs standard training failing beyond 4x4; GSM8K 30% no-intermediate-tokens (vs No-CoT ~17); replicated as the strongest curriculum baseline in Coconut/CODI

papers.title: CODI: Compressing CoT into Continuous Space via Self-Distillation
papers.scale_tested: GPT-2 124M and LLaMA-3.2-1B, LoRA r128/alpha32 bf16, eff. batch 128, AdamW cosine 3% warmup; GSM8k-Aug 385,620 rows, ~40 epochs = ~36h A100-80GB (GPT-2) / ~48h (1B); lr 3e-3 gamma=1 (GPT-2), lr 8e-4 gamma=20 (1B)
papers.core_mechanism: Same model multitasks teacher (question+gold CoT+answer, CE) and student (question + 6 continuous thoughts + answer, CE); L1 loss aligns teacher/student hidden states at the token immediately before the answer across all layers — dense direct supervision of the latent channel's exit state from gold traces
papers.measured_result: GPT-2: 43.7% GSM8K = first implicit CoT to MATCH explicit CoT-SFT (~99% of it); vs Coconut 34.1, iCoT 30.0, No-CoT 19.1. Ablations: remove L1 distillation loss -> 24.5%; separate static teacher -> 27.1% (self-distillation in-model is load-bearing); 6 latents optimal (~avg gold step count). LLaMA-1B OOD: SVAMP 61.1 vs Coconut 48.8. NOTE: LoRA-only training at 1B worked — direct precedent for frozen-base+LoRA

papers.title: Token Assorted: Mixing Latent and Text Tokens for LM Reasoning
papers.scale_tested: Llama-3.2-1B/3B and 3.1-8B fine-tuned on MetaMathQA/DART-Math (~400k+ rows); plus from-scratch small transformer on synthetic maze
papers.core_mechanism: VQ-VAE trained on gold CoT text compresses 16-token chunks into 1 DISCRETE latent code; first m CoT tokens replaced by codes (m randomized per batch); plain cross-entropy on latent codes = fully supervised discrete latent channel, no continuous-space optimization at all
papers.measured_result: Llama-3.2-1B: MATH 14.7 vs CoT 10.5 (+4.2), GSM8K 48.7 vs 42.7 (+6.0); 17% shorter traces. Pause-token baseline at 1B: average 2.1 vs CoT 14.1 — unsupervised latent compute is catastrophic at 1B

papers.title: Think Before You Speak: Training LMs with Pause Tokens
papers.scale_tested: 1B and 130M decoder-only, pretrained on C4, finetuned on 9 downstream tasks
papers.core_mechanism: Learnable <pause> tokens appended to input; output extraction delayed — extra unsupervised parallel compute
papers.measured_result: Gains ONLY when pause-PRETRAINED + pause-finetuned (1B: +18% EM SQuAD, +8% CSQA, +1% GSM8K); adding pauses at FINETUNING-ONLY gives marginal/mixed results — direct negative evidence for bolting unsupervised latent compute onto a pretrained model, which is exactly the HLWM v1-v9 setting

papers.title: Let's Think Dot by Dot: Hidden Computation in Transformers
papers.scale_tested: 34M-param Llama trained from scratch on synthetic 3SUM/2SUM
papers.core_mechanism: Meaningless filler tokens in place of CoT provide parallel width compute
papers.measured_result: Filler tokens solve tasks unsolvable without them, BUT 'learning to use filler tokens is difficult and requires specific, dense supervision to converge' — with plain answer-only supervision they do not get used; theory limits gains to parallelizable (low quantifier-depth) problems

papers.title: Do Latent Tokens Think? Causal and Adversarial Analysis of Coconut
papers.scale_tested: Coconut-style models (GPT-2-scale reproductions), MMLU/HotpotQA shortcut probes
papers.core_mechanism: Steering perturbations on latent vs CoT tokens; biased/OOD shortcut tests
papers.measured_result: Coconut latents show minimal sensitivity to steering (not reasoning-critical) and the model exploits dataset artifacts — latents behave as placeholders/compute slots, not content carriers. Passing an accuracy gate does not certify a working content channel; keep the masked-premise necessity test as headline

papers.title: Towards Inference-time Scaling for Continuous Space Reasoning
papers.scale_tested: Coconut GPT-2 backbone, GSM8K-scale data
papers.core_mechanism: Dropout-based sampling of diverse latent trajectories + PRM/ORM reranking ported from discrete space
papers.measured_result: Pass@N headroom exists, but discrete-space PRM/ORM recipes unlock only MARGINAL gains: latent representations of correct vs incorrect thoughts are geometrically indiscriminable — continuous thoughts lack inductive biases for scoring/diversity. Explains HLWM lanes' cosine 0.94-0.98 collapse: diversity does not emerge, it must be imposed

papers.title: DEMix Layers: Disentangling Domains for Modular LM
papers.scale_tested: Autoregressive transformers 125M -> 1.3B, multi-domain corpora
papers.core_mechanism: Expert FFNs conditioned on DOMAIN METADATA — routing is supervised/deterministic at train time, parameter-free weighted ensemble at inference; no learned router, no balance loss
papers.measured_result: Lower test perplexity than dense at 125M-1.3B, experts addable/removable without retraining; replicated small-scale evidence that label-conditioned expert specialization works where learned routing fails

papers.title: MoE Routing Testbed: Expert Specialization and Routing at Small Scale
papers.scale_tested: Small-scale LMs (testbed explicitly built because routing methods are indistinguishable at small size), validated up to 35x larger
papers.core_mechanism: Reference router prescribing ideal routing from known domain labels = measurable upper bound for specialization; compares learned routers against it
papers.measured_result: Many routing techniques exhibit similar (weak) behavior at small scale; 'balancing scope' is the crucial factor for specialization + utilization; domain-label reference routing is the well-defined upper bound — i.e., at our scale the label-supervised router IS the evidence-backed design, learned routing is not

papers.title: Parallel Scaling Law for Language Models (PARSCALE)
papers.scale_tested: 0.5B-4.4B from scratch on 42B tokens (Pile); 1.8B on 1T tokens two-stage (ParScale stage = 20B tokens); PEFT on frozen Qwen-2.5-3B (prefixes+aggregation only) on Stack-V2
papers.core_mechanism: P parallel streams = P different LEARNED PREFIXES (prefix-tuning; random init suffices to break symmetry) through shared frozen/joint weights, outputs merged by dynamic MLP-weighted softmax aggregation — differentiation via input prefixes + output competition, NOT diversity penalties
papers.measured_result: P=8 at 1.8B: +34% relative GSM8K, +23% MMLU at identical data; loss scales like O(log P) parameter increase; works with FROZEN backbone via PEFT — but the cheapest demonstrated budget is 20B tokens (stage 2), ~5 orders above ours

papers.title: A Silver Bullet or a Compromise? Comprehensive Study of Gist-Token Context Compression
papers.scale_tested: Llama-3-8B-scale gist/compression models (plus survey of ICAE-7B, AutoCompressor OPT-2.7B@2B tokens, Gisting LLaMA-7B@~130k instructions)
papers.core_mechanism: Soft gist tokens replace full context; probing localizes where content dies
papers.measured_result: Near-lossless on fuzzy tasks but <20% accuracy on precise synthetic recall at high compression; probing shows the bottleneck is IN the gist representations (info present upstream, unusable downstream — the exact HLWM probe-0.30/generation-0.000 signature); proposed fix = fine-grained AUTOENCODING loss forcing reconstruction of original tokens. No positive prefix-content-transfer result exists below 2.7B params

lenses.recipe: PRINCIPLE (uniform across all 12 papers): at <=1B, latent components work ONLY when every latent position receives dense, teacher-aligned supervision derived from gold traces; nothing works by emergence at finetune time. HLWM's unique asset — free gold traces for every synthetic row — is precisely the ingredient v1-v9 never fed to the latents. CHANNEL (highest-evidence bet, CODI recipe): delete the 42-token pooled workspace prefix. Student pass = question + <bot> + 6 continuous thoughts (last hidden state -> 2-layer MLP projection -> next input embedding, NO gate, NO zero-init, NO KL-to-base) + <eot> + answer, CE on answer. Teacher pass (SAME weights, same batch) = question + gold trace + answer, CE on trace+answer. Distillation loss = L1 between student and teacher hidden states at the token immediately preceding the answer, summed over all layers, normalized by teacher hidden-state std; total L = CE_t + CE_s + gamma*L1 with gamma tuned so the L1 gradient magnitude ~ CE (CODI: gamma=1 at 124M, gamma=20 at 1B LoRA; start 10 at 0.6B, sweep {5,20} in smoke runs). Set thought count = median gold-trace step count per family (CODI found 6 = avg steps optimal; 42 is unsupported). AdamW, cosine, 3% warmup, lr 5e-4..8e-4 on LoRA, effective batch >=64 (grad-accum 16; keeps ~800 optimizer steps of 3200-step budget after 2x teacher-pass cost). CODI-1B used LoRA r128/alpha32 — raise rank from 16 toward 64-128 on attn+MLP if VRAM allows. Keep the masked-premise rows as the headline necessity gate; add CODI's decode-the-thoughts probe (nearest-vocab decoding of each latent should show intermediate quantities). Optional discrete alternative if continuous fails smoke test: Token-Assorted-lite — cluster (k-means, no VQ-VAE training) hidden encodings of gold-trace chunks into 512 codes, extend vocab, CE-supervise latent codes directly with randomized text/latent mixing. EXPERTS/ROUTING (feasible, re-scoped): abandon learned routing at this scale — 3/3 HLWM collapses match the literature norm. Experts = 2 LoRA branches assigned to family GROUPS; train with hard label-conditioned routing (DEMix-style metadata routing) so experts are forced disjoint by construction; router = linear classifier on mean-pooled question hidden state trained with CE on family labels (weight 0.25), used only at eval via argmax. Gates: held-out router acc >=0.95; expert-swap ablation (family-A rows through expert B) must drop accuracy; no load-balance loss, no orthogonality penalty (Expert Race 2503.16057 shows balance losses cannot prevent functional collapse anyway). LANES (demote to exploratory or cut): the only mechanism with any positive evidence is PARSCALE — P=2 learned RANDOM-INIT prefix sets (never zero-init: symmetry must be broken at step 0) through the shared model, merged by a dynamic MLP-softmax output aggregator, PLUS per-lane supervised auxiliary targets from gold traces (lane 1: CE on the extraction sub-trace; lane 2: CE on the computation sub-trace; weight 0.2 each) so diversity is imposed by disjoint supervision, not penalized into existence; report lane cosine as telemetry only, never as a gate. Budget allocation if anything slips: channel > routing > lanes; lanes are the preregistered first cut.
lenses.feasibility_at_our_budget: MIXED, mechanism by mechanism. CHANNEL: the mechanism (latent CoT with dense gold-trace supervision) is replicated at 124M-1B by 4 independent groups (Coconut, iCoT, CODI, Token Assorted), and CODI's 1B run is LoRA-only on a frozen-ish base — directly analogous to our setup. BUT every success consumed vastly more data-compute: CODI = 385k rows x 40 epochs (~15.4M row-passes, 36-48 A100-h); Coconut's synthetic-task wins used 9-18k unique rows (our regime!) but ~50 epochs (~300-900k row-passes). Our budget is ~12.8k row-passes (3200 steps x accum 4), halved again by the teacher pass -> ~6-10k. That is 2-3 orders below any demonstrated success. Mitigations that are real but unproven in combination: our families are far narrower than GSM8K, our 0.6B base is far stronger than GPT-2, and 6 latents (not 42) shrinks the learning problem. Honest call: CODI-style channel at this budget is a plausible-but-undemonstrated extrapolation — preregister a mid-run go/no-go (masked-row acc must be >0 by step ~1600, since CODI's signal appears early) and a fallback to the abstention-only claim. ROUTING: comfortably feasible ONLY as label-supervised/metadata routing (DEMix worked at 125M; a 4-way family classifier on 7.5k rows is trivial); learned emergent routing has no small-scale positive evidence and should not be retried. LANES: NOT feasible as an emergent mechanism — PARSCALE's cheapest demonstration is 20B tokens; either run the supervised-decomposition variant as explicitly exploratory or cut lanes. Net: v10 can realistically demonstrate channel (with the gap flagged) + supervised routing; it cannot honestly promise all three.
risks: Data-compute gap: all positive latent-channel results used 30x-1000x more row-passes (CODI ~15.4M vs our ~6-10k after teacher overhead); no paper demonstrates CODI-style distillation converging in <2 epochs of <=50k rows — this is the single biggest extrapolation in the recipe

LoRA capacity: CODI's only <=1B LoRA success used r128/alpha32; our r16 may be too thin for all-layer hidden-state alignment — if rank cannot be raised, the distillation loss may plateau (watch L1 loss vs CE ratio early)

Curriculum/hyperparameter fragility is replicated: Coconut w/o curriculum scores BELOW No-CoT (14.4 vs 16.5), CODI w/o the L1 term drops 43.7->24.5, gamma differs 20x between 124M and 1B — a single bad gamma/lr choice reproduces a v9-style null and is indistinguishable from 'mechanism dead' without the preregistered mid-run probe

Pseudo-reasoning confound: 2512.21711 shows Coconut-style latents can pass accuracy gates as shortcut placeholders; only the masked-premise necessity gate distinguishes a real channel from an artifact exploiter — it must stay headline even if it makes the run fail

Claim scope on routing: label-supervised routing demonstrates modularity, NOT learned routing; writing it up as 'experts work' without the re-scope would overclaim relative to DEMix/testbed evidence that learned routers are indistinguishable at small scale

Lanes have zero <=1B low-data positive evidence (PARSCALE minimum = 20B tokens; 2510.12167 shows latent diversity does not emerge); shipping lanes as a gated claim invites failure #10 — preregister them as exploratory or cut

lenses.lens: Data engineering for reasoning distillation at small scale (STaR/rationalization, process vs outcome supervision, trace formats, internalization/compression, difficulty curriculum, dataset-size scaling)

papers.title: CODI: Compressing Chain-of-Thought into Continuous Space via Self-Distillation
papers.scale_tested: GPT-2 (124M) and LLaMA-3.2-1B-Instruct; GSM8k-Aug 385k rows (equation-only traces, NL stripped); LoRA r128 alpha32 bf16, eff. batch 128, warmup 3%; GPT-2: lr 3e-3, gamma=1, 40 epochs, ~36h on 1xA100-80GB; LLaMA-1B: lr 8e-4, gamma=20, 10 epochs, ~48h on 1xA100-80GB
papers.core_mechanism: One model jointly trained on teacher task (explicit CoT CE) and student task (question + 6 continuous thoughts, last-hidden fed back as next input embedding, then answer CE); L1 distillation loss aligns student vs teacher hidden states ACROSS ALL LAYERS at one designated pre-answer token, per-layer normalized by teacher batch std. Dense direct supervision of the latent — no emergence needed.
papers.measured_result: GPT-2 GSM8k 43.7% ~= explicit CoT at 3.1x token compression, +28.2% over prior implicit-CoT SOTA; No-CoT-SFT baseline 19.1%. Ablations: remove L1 loss -> 24.5%; independent static teacher -> 27.1%; remove projection -> 42.5% (nearly free).

papers.title: Training Large Language Models to Reason in a Continuous Latent Space (Coconut)
papers.scale_tested: GPT-2 (124M); GSM8k-Aug 385,620 rows, ProntoQA 9,000 rows, ProsQA 17,886 rows; lr 1e-4, eff. batch 128; initial stage 6 epochs + 3 epochs per curriculum stage (math: c=2 latents/step, 3 stages + final; logic: c=1, 6 stages); optimizer reset at each stage switch
papers.core_mechanism: Stage-k training replaces the first k gold CoT steps with c continuous thoughts (bounded by <bot>/<eot>); the gold trace is the curriculum scaffold that teaches the latent channel step-by-step before removing language.
papers.measured_result: GSM8k 34.1 (CoT 42.9, No-CoT 16.5, iCoT 30.0, pause-token 16.4 = no better than No-CoT); WITHOUT curriculum 14.4 — curriculum is the whole effect. ProntoQA 99.8 (9k rows), ProsQA 97.0 vs CoT 77.5 (17.9k rows): latent reasoning BEAT explicit CoT on synthetic structured tasks at exactly our row scale.

papers.title: From Explicit CoT to Implicit CoT: Learning to Internalize CoT Step by Step (ICoT-SI)
papers.scale_tested: GPT-2 Small/Medium, Phi-3 3.8B, Mistral-7B; multiplication 808k rows, GSM8K-aug 378k rows; batch 32, lr 5e-5, linear token-removal schedule Delta tokens/epoch (Delta=8 mult, Delta=1 GSM8K on GPT-2), optimizer reset when schedule advances; tens of epochs
papers.core_mechanism: Start from an explicit-CoT-finetuned model; delete CoT tokens from the front on a linear per-epoch schedule and keep finetuning, forcing internalization into hidden states.
papers.measured_result: GPT-2 Small: 9x9 multiplication up to 99% with zero emitted steps (standard no-CoT training fails beyond 4x4); Mistral-7B >50% GSM8K with no intermediate tokens. Delta=16 (too-fast removal) fails to converge — removal rate is the critical hyperparameter.

papers.title: Implicit Chain of Thought Reasoning via Knowledge Distillation (ICoT-KD)
papers.scale_tested: GPT-2 Small/Medium teacher-student; multi-digit multiplication + GSM8K (aug corpus later reused as GSM8k-Aug 385k)
papers.core_mechanism: 'Vertical' distillation: teacher's per-step hidden states (from explicit CoT positions) are distilled into the student's hidden states across layers, so reasoning happens layer-wise instead of token-wise.
papers.measured_result: Enabled tasks unsolvable without explicit CoT at no-CoT speed, but underperforms both explicit CoT and later methods (CODI beats prior implicit SOTA by 28.2%; iCoT line reported ~22% GSM8K at GPT-2-medium). Establishes hidden-state alignment works but token-level L1 (CODI) > full-trajectory state matching.

papers.title: STaR: Self-Taught Reasoner (Bootstrapping Reasoning With Reasoning)
papers.scale_tested: GPT-J 6B; CommonsenseQA (~9.7k train), GSM8K (7.5k train), arithmetic; few outer loops of sample->filter->finetune-from-scratch
papers.core_mechanism: Loop: few-shot sample rationales; keep those whose final answer is correct; for failures, 'rationalization' — regenerate with the gold answer as a hint and keep those traces; finetune on the union; repeat.
papers.measured_result: CQA 72.5% vs 73.0% for a fine-tuned 30x larger model (GPT-3) and vs 60% direct-answer finetune. Rationalization is what covers hard rows the model can't solve unaided — with a gold-trace generator we get its benefit for free with zero sampling.

papers.title: Distilling Step-by-Step! Outperforming Larger Language Models with Less Training Data and Smaller Model Sizes
papers.scale_tested: T5 220M / 770M / 11B students; e-SNLI, ANLI, CQA, SVAMP; teacher rationales from 540B PaLM
papers.core_mechanism: Multi-task SFT: answer-prediction CE + rationale-generation CE as two prefixed tasks (rationale as extra supervision signal, NOT required at inference).
papers.measured_result: 770M T5 beats few-shot 540B PaLM using only 80% of data where standard finetuning fails at 100%; at 220M, beats standard finetuning trained on the FULL dataset while using as little as 12.5% of e-SNLI. Direct evidence rationale-as-auxiliary-loss multiplies per-row signal at 220-770M.

papers.title: Small Models Struggle to Learn from Strong Reasoners (Small Model Learnability Gap / Mix Distillation)
papers.scale_tested: Students Qwen2.5-0.5B/1.5B/3B/7B/14B/32B + Llama-3.2-1B/3B/8B/70B Instruct; SFT on 7.5k MATH rows; long-CoT (QwQ-32B) vs short-CoT (Qwen2.5-32B) teachers
papers.core_mechanism: Measures long-vs-short trace and big-vs-small teacher effects as a function of student size; Mix-Long = 1:4 long:short blend.
papers.measured_result: Qwen2.5-0.5B: long-CoT 14.8 vs short-CoT 19.5 (Delta = -4.7, short WINS); 1.5B: -7.1; crossover only at ~7B. Large-teacher traces also hurt at 0.5-1.5B. Mix-Long recovers >8 pts at 3B. At our exact 0.6B/7.5k-row regime: traces must be SHORT and simple.

papers.title: TokenSkip: Controllable Chain-of-Thought Compression in LLMs
papers.scale_tested: Qwen2.5-Instruct 3B/7B/14B, LLaMA-3.1-8B; 7,473 GSM8K rows (+7.5k MATH); LoRA r8 alpha16, lr 5e-5 cosine, warmup 0.1, 3 epochs; ~2h (7B) / 2.5h (14B) on two RTX 3090s
papers.core_mechanism: Prune low-importance CoT tokens offline at sampled ratios gamma in {0.5..1.0}; train with the ratio as a control token so one model serves any compression level — a trace-length curriculum inside a single SFT pass, no stage switching.
papers.measured_result: 14B: 40% token reduction (313->181) with <0.4% accuracy drop. 3B: gamma=0.9 -0.5, gamma=0.7 -3.6, gamma=0.5 -9.3 pts — smaller models tolerate markedly less compression. Whole recipe fits a budget nearly identical to ours (7.4k rows, LoRA, ~2 GPU-h).

papers.title: TinyGSM: achieving >80% on GSM8k with small language models
papers.scale_tested: 1.3B Phi-family generator + separate 1.3B verifier; 12.3M synthetic GSM problems with Python solutions generated by GPT-3.5
papers.core_mechanism: Massive high-quality synthetic data + best-of-N selection by a small trained verifier (verifier scores candidates; top-1 picked).
papers.measured_result: 81.5% GSM8K, beating 34B models and the GPT-3.5 teacher (77.4%). Verifier gain is robust at 1.3B — consistent with HLWM's own finding that scoring heads are the component that works — but the generator needed 12.3M rows, ~250-1600x our budget: generation quality at ~1B is data-hungry; selection is not.

papers.title: Math-Shepherd: Verify and Reinforce LLMs Step-by-step without Human Annotations
papers.scale_tested: 7B PRM (Mistral-7B/Llemma-7B); GSM8K + MATH; process labels auto-built via Monte-Carlo completion rollouts from each step (hard estimation), no runs below 7B
papers.core_mechanism: Per-step correctness labels estimated by whether completions from that step reach the gold answer; PRM trained on these labels, used for best-of-N reranking and step-PPO.
papers.measured_result: Mistral-7B GSM8K 77.9 -> 84.1 with step-PPO, 89.1 with PRM verification. For HLWM the expensive part (MC label estimation) is free: the synthetic generator emits exact per-step values, so gold process labels for verifier heads cost nothing. No <=1B PRM evidence though.

papers.title: DAPO: An Open-Source LLM Reinforcement Learning System at Scale (dynamic sampling / pass-rate filtering)
papers.scale_tested: Qwen2.5-32B base, large-scale RLVR (AIME math); no small-scale runs
papers.core_mechanism: Dynamic sampling drops prompts whose group pass rate is 0 or 1 (zero advantage/zero gradient), keeping only the informative middle difficulty band — the formal basis for pass-rate banding ~0.2-0.8.
papers.measured_result: 50 points AIME-2024 at 32B with the filtered band among the four load-bearing techniques. Banding evidence is ONLY at 32B RL; at 0.6B SFT treat banding as a data-selection heuristic (HLWM v9.0's frozen-base pass@32 banding already implements it), not a validated result.

papers.title: Specializing Smaller Language Models towards Multi-Step Reasoning
papers.scale_tested: FlanT5 250M/760M/3B/11B students; CoT distilled from code-davinci-002 (>=175B) on GSM8K-family augmented data (~130k chains); full finetuning
papers.core_mechanism: Concentrate all of a small model's capacity on one task family (specialization): distill teacher CoT in multiple formats (in-context + zero-shot mixes), accept loss of generic ability (BigBench drops) to lift the math scaling curve.
papers.measured_result: Lifts the multi-step-math scaling curve of <=3B models above their generalist baselines while BigBench-Hard degrades; format mixing and starting from an instruction-tuned checkpoint (Flan) are reported as decisive design choices. Supports HLWM's frozen-instruct-base + narrow-family setup; exact deltas are per-figure, modest at 250-760M.

lenses.recipe: V10 CHANNEL = CODI one-stage self-distillation on gold traces (replaces all emergence hopes with a dense loss the literature shows is load-bearing). GENERATOR EMITS PER ROW: (1) gold compact trace in GSM8k-Aug format — equation-only, NL stripped, steps delimited as <<a op b = c>>, <=3 steps and <=30 trace tokens (Learnability Gap: at 0.5B short beats long by 4.7 pts; CODI/iCoT both trained on exactly this stripped format); (2) per-step intermediate values c_k as literals; (3) premise literals (keep v9 masking machinery for necessity audits); (4) TokenSkip-style compressed trace variants at gamma in {1.0, 0.7, 0.4} tagged with a ratio control token (in-batch length curriculum, no stage switches or optimizer resets — Coconut/iCoT-SI multi-stage curricula need 20+ epochs we cannot afford); (5) one single-step-corrupted trace per row with the corrupted step index (gold Math-Shepherd process labels for the verifier head, zero MC rollouts); (6) difficulty knobs (chain len 1-3, digits, distractors) + frozen-base pass@32, train/audit band 0.2-0.8 with ~20% easy rows kept for stability; (7) N-best candidates + correctness for the proven abstention stack. LOSSES: L = CE_teacher(question + gold trace + answer) + CE_student(question + 6 latent thoughts + answer) + gamma * L1(h_student, h_teacher) at ONE designated pre-answer token (must be a real Qwen3 token, e.g. the ':' of 'Answer:'; never bos/eos — v8 lesson), across all layers, each layer normalized by teacher batch std; alpha=beta=1, gamma=20 (CODI's 1B value; their 124M used 1 — sweep {5,20} only if a pilot fits), + 0.3 * CE per-latent value-decode head where latent pair k must decode step-k value ONLY (this is the LANES fix: supervised distinct targets instead of diversity penalties — extrapolation, flag it), + 0.1 * router CE on family id if experts are retained (supervised routing instead of load-balance penalties — extrapolation). Latent thoughts: 6, fed back as input embeddings between <bot>/<eot> (CODI 3.1x compression on ~20-token traces). HYPERPARAMETERS: LoRA r128 alpha32 all layers if VRAM allows (CODI's setting; disclose deviation if staying r16), lr 8e-4 cosine, 3% warmup, joint teacher+student costs ~1.8x per step so expect ~1800-2200 steps in 6.5h; pack short rows / raise grad-accum toward 16-32 (CODI/Coconut used eff. batch 128; our 4 is the largest unforced deviation from every successful run). DATA: emit 25k rows, consume single-epoch whatever fits (~8-16k); do NOT trade rows for long traces. GATES: (a) student (no-trace) accuracy vs a No-CoT-SFT control trained on identical rows/steps — the CODI analogue of 43.7 vs 19.1; (b) necessity certificate = retrain-or-ablate without the L1 term must drop materially (CODI: 43.7 -> 24.5), replacing inert-gate telemetry; (c) per-latent value-decode accuracy per lane (distinctness is now a supervised metric, not a cosine hope).
lenses.feasibility_at_our_budget: Split verdict. ROWS: yes — Coconut hit 99.8%/97.0% on ProntoQA (9k rows) and ProsQA (17.9k rows), TokenSkip used 7.4k rows + LoRA + ~2 GPU-h, Learnability Gap used 7.5k rows on Qwen2.5-0.5B; our 7.5k-50k synthetic rows are squarely in the evidenced range for synthetic structured tasks. MODEL SIZE: yes — CODI/Coconut/iCoT-SI all work at GPT-2 124M and CODI at 1B, bracketing 0.6B. COMPUTE: this is the honest gap — every successful internalization run used 2e5 to 1.5e7 example-presentations (Coconut ProntoQA ~24 epochs x 9k x batch-128 schedule; CODI 385k x 40 epochs, 36 A100-h at 124M and 48 A100-h at 1B) versus our ~8-13k presentations at eff. batch 4 in 6.5 T4-h, i.e. 1.5-3 orders of magnitude less optimization. Two things plausibly close it: our task families (1-3 step chains) are far simpler than GSM8K and closer to ProntoQA, and Qwen3-0.6B-instruct already performs explicit CoT, so the teacher task starts near-converged (GPT-2 had to learn CoT from scratch — most of those 40 epochs). Realistic expectation: a scaled-down but auditable effect — gate on the w/o-L1 ablation gap and on beating the matched No-CoT-SFT control, not on absolute parity with explicit CoT. The channel fix is well-evidenced; the supervised-lanes and supervised-router fixes are principled extrapolations of the same dense-supervision result, not literature-tested, and should carry weaker preregistered claims.
risks: Presentation-count gap: all successful internalization runs used effective batch 128 and 10-40 epochs; at batch-1 x grad-accum-4 x ~2000 joint steps we have 100-1000x fewer presentations — the single most likely failure mode. Mitigate with sequence packing / grad-accum 16+, or the result may be noise.

No published CODI/Coconut run at <=25k rows on math-style tasks: the 9k/17.9k successes are ProntoQA/ProsQA (pure symbolic search); GSM8k-style arithmetic used 385k rows. Our arithmetic families sit between these; row-sufficiency is inferred, not measured.

CODI's L1-across-all-layers alignment assumes teacher and student share trainable weights at every layer; with a frozen base the alignment gradient flows only through LoRA + custom modules — the ablation gate (w/o-L1 drop) must be preregistered to detect a silently dead loss, HLWM's recurring failure signature.

Designated-token choice on Qwen3: no BOS, bos aliases to eos (v8 root cause). The alignment token and <bot>/<eot> latents must be verified real, non-boundary token ids under the actual tokenizer before launch.

Supervised router (family-id CE) and supervised lane targets (per-step value decode) have no direct literature support at any scale under this lens — they are extrapolations of CODI's dense-supervision result; preregister them as secondary claims so their failure cannot sink the channel claim.

Pass-rate banding 0.2-0.8 is evidenced only at 7B-32B RLVR (DAPO); at 0.6B SFT it may discard the easy rows that Coconut-style latent training needs early — keep a ~20% easy stratum rather than a hard band.

lenses.lens: Making the selective-prediction win statistically significant: AUGRC methodology, paired power analysis, variance reduction, and the 2024-2026 abstention baselines the conformal score must beat

papers.title: Overcoming Common Flaws in the Evaluation of Selective Classification Systems (AUGRC)
papers.scale_tested: 6 image datasets (CIFAR-10/100, SVHN, iWildCam, BREEDS, CAMELYON-17), 13 confidence scoring functions, 2-10 training inits per dataset; test sets thousands of rows; no LLMs
papers.core_mechanism: AUGRC = average risk of UNDETECTED failures over all working points; key identity (Appendix A.1.2): AUGRC = (1-AUROC_f)*acc*(1-acc) + 0.5*(1-acc)^2, so when two abstention scores rank the SAME predictions (identical correctness labels), delta-AUGRC = -acc*(1-acc)*delta-AUROC_f — the comparison reduces exactly to a paired AUROC test on failure labels. Their own significance protocol: 500 bootstrap resamples of the test set, one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank on pairwise CSF comparisons, Holm correction for FWER at 5%
papers.measured_result: AUGRC changes top-3 method rankings on 5/6 datasets vs AURC; ranking stability certified via Wilcoxon+Holm on 500 bootstraps; metric bounded [0, 1/2]

papers.title: A Novel Characterization of the Population AURC and Rates of Finite Sample Estimators
papers.scale_tested: CIFAR/ImageNet-scale classifiers, multiple CSFs; theory + Monte Carlo; no LLMs
papers.core_mechanism: Population AURC as a reweighted risk; plug-in weight estimators consistent with low bias/MSE
papers.measured_result: Plug-in estimators converge at O(sqrt(ln(n)/n)) — at our n=288 the sampling noise term sqrt(ln(288)/288)≈0.14 in normalized units, i.e. small-n AURC/AUGRC estimates carry non-negligible bias+variance; no closed-form CI provided (must bootstrap/DeLong)

papers.title: Adding Error Bars to Evals: A Statistical Approach to Language Model Evaluations
papers.scale_tested: Methodology paper (Anthropic); formulas validated on standard evals (MATH, HumanEval, MGSM); model-size agnostic
papers.core_mechanism: Question-level PAIRED differences (exploits cross-model correlation to shrink SE); clustered SEs when rows are drawn in related groups (our family x difficulty strata); K resamples per question to kill conditional variance; sample-size formula n = (z_{alpha/2}+z_beta)^2 * (omega^2 + sigma_A^2/K_A + sigma_B^2/K_B) / delta^2 where omega^2 = Var(x_A)+Var(x_B)-2Cov(x_A,x_B)
papers.measured_result: Worked example: omega^2=1/9, delta=0.03, alpha=0.05, power 0.8 -> n≈969 questions; raising K from 1 to 10 at n=198 cuts MDE from 13.2% to 7.5%

papers.title: An Empirical Investigation of Statistical Significance in NLP
papers.scale_tested: Large collections of real system outputs across MT/parsing/tagging test sets (hundreds to thousands of rows)
papers.core_mechanism: Canonical paired bootstrap for system comparison; significance threshold depends on test-set size and system similarity — more-correlated systems reach significance at smaller gains
papers.measured_result: Gain-vs-significance curves per task; standard implementation is 10^4-10^5 resamples; directly the test family our win-fraction statistic approximates (win fraction f ≈ 1 - one-sided bootstrap p, so our preregistered 0.80 bar was equivalent to demanding only p<=0.20)

papers.title: With Little Power Comes Great Responsibility
papers.scale_tested: Meta-analysis of GLUE/SQuAD leaderboards: 119 accuracy comparisons, 57 SOTA claims across 14 papers
papers.core_mechanism: Power analysis for NLP comparisons; MDE at 80% power vs typical claimed gains
papers.measured_result: Typical claimed gains are BELOW the MDE of the test sets used: MRPC (n=1,725) MDE +1.62% vs typical gain +0.63%; SST-2 (n=1,821) MDE +1.02% vs +0.57%; WNLI (n=147) MDE +5.26%. Even ~1.8k-row test sets cannot certify sub-point gains — our 288-row audit is far under-powered for a 0.003-0.004 AUGRC effect

papers.title: Resolution Diagnostics for Paired LLM Evaluation
papers.scale_tested: Open LLM Leaderboard v1 (40 pairwise comparisons) and MMLU-Pro top-10 (9 adjacent pairs); public eval data
papers.core_mechanism: Inverts level-alpha power-(1-beta) paired tests to a resolution ratio q = N/N*; handles clustering; supports anytime-valid sequential extension of audits across sessions
papers.measured_result: 11/40 and 4/9 displayed rankings unresolved at (0.05, 0.8); unpaired Cohen-h+(1-rho) shortcut wrong by ~2x in the close-comparison regime (3/5 off-the-shelf calculators inherit the error) — use the paired formula, not G*Power defaults

papers.title: Detecting hallucinations in large language models using semantic entropy
papers.scale_tested: LLaMA-2-70B/13B/7B, Falcon-40B, Mistral-7B, GPT-4; 5 QA datasets + biography generation; 10 samples/question + DeBERTa entailment clustering (5-10x inference cost)
papers.core_mechanism: Entropy over semantically-clustered samples (bidirectional entailment); discrete variant works from sample counts alone
papers.measured_result: Beats P(True) and logprob baselines on AUROC and AURAC averaged over 5 datasets; highest selective accuracy at >80% answer rate. CRITICAL for us: with short synthetic numeric/unit answers, clustering degenerates to normalized exact match, so DISCRETE semantic entropy over our existing N=8 pool costs ~0 extra GPU and must be a preregistered baseline

papers.title: Semantic Entropy Probes: Robust and Cheap Hallucination Detection in LLMs
papers.scale_tested: Llama-2-7B/70B, Llama-3-70B, Mistral-7B, Phi-3; TriviaQA/SQuAD/BioASQ/NQ; linear probes on hidden states (train cost ~minutes CPU)
papers.core_mechanism: Linear probe on mid-to-late-layer hidden states (second-last token) predicting binarized semantic entropy of a single generation — no sampling at test time
papers.measured_result: AUROC 0.7-0.95 depending on setting; below full SE but above accuracy probes OOD; smallest model 7B — untested at 0.6B, but the probe recipe is directly trainable in our pipeline as a cheap baseline/feature

papers.title: Language Models (Mostly) Know What They Know (P(True))
papers.scale_tested: Anthropic models 800M/3B/12B/52B, 850B pretraining tokens; TriviaQA, GSM8K, codegen, etc.
papers.core_mechanism: Self-evaluation P(True) of proposed answers, boosted by showing T=1 samples; P(IK) probes
papers.measured_result: Self-evaluation AUROC improves monotonically with size and is weak at the 800M scale (smaller models excluded because they 'perform poorly'); zero-shot P(True) poorly calibrated except at 52B. Implication: P(True) at 0.6B is a cheap but expected-weak baseline — include it, but semantic entropy and the verifier heads are the real competition

papers.title: Mitigating LLM Hallucinations via Conformal Abstention
papers.scale_tested: Gemini Pro; TriviaQA (short answers) + Temporal Sequences (long answers); CRC/RCPS calibration on held-out sets of a few hundred-1k rows
papers.core_mechanism: Conformal risk control on a self-consistency/match-count score; abstention threshold with distribution-free bound on hallucination rate
papers.measured_result: Bounds hallucination rate as targeted; beats logprob-based scores on abstention rate for long-form (comparable on TriviaQA short answers) — direct precedent that conformal-calibrated agreement scores beat max-logprob, matching our directional result; note their wins concentrate on LONG answers, ours are short-form (harder to beat logprob)

papers.title: Comparing the Areas under Two or More Correlated ROC Curves: A Nonparametric Approach (DeLong)
papers.scale_tested: Classical; exact for any n via U-statistic theory; power depends on n_fail*n_success and score correlation
papers.core_mechanism: Analytic paired variance for the difference of two AUROCs computed on the SAME labels via per-row structural components — the correct confirmatory test once delta-AUGRC is reduced to delta-AUROC_f through the Traub identity (identical predictions, only the score differs)
papers.measured_result: Uniformly more powerful than unpaired comparison when scores are positively correlated (ours are: both consume logprob-family features); standard in every stats package

papers.title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to Testing Statistical Significance in NLP
papers.scale_tested: Survey/protocol over standard NLP test sets
papers.core_mechanism: Decision procedure for test selection: sign/Wilcoxon/permutation for unknown distributions, paired bootstrap for complex metrics (curve integrals like AUGRC qualify)
papers.measured_result: Protocol adopted widely; endorses paired permutation (sign-flip on per-row pairs) as exact-level alternative to bootstrap for non-decomposable metrics

lenses.recipe:
V10 ABSTENTION-CLAIM STATISTICAL PACKAGE (zero training-GPU cost; the budget is audit rows).

(0) Diagnosis of v9: bootstrap win fraction f is a one-sided p-value in disguise (p ≈ 1-f). The preregistered 0.80 bar demanded only p<=0.20; the observed f=0.746/0.792 means per-seed z = PHI^-1(f) = 0.66/0.81 at n=288, Stouffer-pooled z = (0.66+0.81)/sqrt(2) = 1.04. The effect is real-looking but the design can only detect effects ~2.8x larger (MDE multiplier = 2.93/1.04) at alpha=0.05/90% power.

(1) PRIMARY PREREGISTERED TEST — reduce delta-AUGRC to paired failure-AUROC. Both abstention scores (5-feature conformal combiner vs max-logprob) rank the IDENTICAL selected answers with identical correctness labels, so by Traub et al. Eq. 8: delta-AUGRC = -acc(1-acc) * delta-AUROC_f. Preregister: H1: AUROC_f(conformal) > AUROC_f(logprob), one-sided paired DeLong per seed on the FULL audit set (full AUGRC, not partial — partial discards rows and power); pool seeds with fixed-effect Stouffer z_pool=(z17+z29)/sqrt(2); reject at z_pool >= 1.645. Report the headline in AUGRC units via the identity (observed v9 effects 0.0028/0.0041 AUGRC ↔ delta-AUROC_f ≈ 0.013/0.020 at acc≈0.7). Secondary (descriptive + robustness): stratified paired bootstrap of delta-AUGRC, B=10,000, resampling rows within family x difficulty-band strata with both scores moving together per row, report BCa 90% CI — never a bare win fraction again; if a bar is kept it must be f >= 0.95 (= p <= 0.05).

(2) SAMPLE SIZE (Miller Eq. 9 applied to the observed effect, conservative = pooled z 1.04 at 576 total rows): n_total = 576 * ((z_alpha + z_beta)/1.04)^2. Targets: alpha=0.05/90% power -> 4,540 total (2,270/seed); alpha=0.05/80% -> 3,280 total (1,640/seed); minimum honest option, clearing the old 0.80 bar with 90% assurance -> 2,390 total (1,195/seed). PREREGISTER n=1,152 fresh audit rows/seed (4 families x 3 bands x 96), plus reclamation below, and state achieved power (~80% at alpha=0.05 pooled) and the MDE explicitly; a null is reported as 'no effect larger than MDE', not 'no difference'.

(3) FREE VARIANCE REDUCTION: (a) Cross-conformal reclamation — replace the 96/64/96 dedicated calibration split with 5-fold nested cross-conformal (each row's publish decision and score computed by folds that never calibrated on it; k=floor((n_fold+1)(1-c)) per fold, c=0.35): all ~544 existing rows/seed become audit-eligible, a free ~1.9x. (b) Stratify audit sampling by family x difficulty band and use clustered/stratified SEs (Miller App. A/C). (c) Difficulty mix: allocate bands so selected-answer accuracy lands near 0.5-0.65 on the audit stratum — acc(1-acc) and n_fail*n_success both maximize AUROC_f precision; preregister the stratified population as the estimand and also report the natural mix. (d) Anytime-valid extension: preregister a sequential e-process (mixture sequential z-test) so a second audit session can be appended without alpha spending (per 2605.30315's sequential-testing framing).

(4) SESSION PLAN: the abstention power audit is INFERENCE-ONLY (reuse v10 checkpoints; no training). Measured v9 throughput ~37 s/row/GPU at N=8 pool; cap audit-row max_new_tokens at 96 and use programmatic graders only -> target <=30 s/row -> 1,152 rows/seed ≈ 9.6h with seeds parallel on the 2xT4, inside one 12h session on the ~30h of freed quota (fallback: one seed per account/session). Keep N=8 — the agreement feature and semantic-entropy baseline both need the pool.

(5) BASELINE FAMILY (the win must survive 2024-2026 baselines, all computable from artifacts already generated): confirmatory comparison = max-logprob (uncorrected, alpha=0.05). Secondary family with Holm correction (as in Traub et al.): length-normalized sequence logprob; token-level predictive entropy; DISCRETE SEMANTIC ENTROPY over the N=8 pool via normalized-exact-match clustering (near-zero cost for short synthetic answers — this is the strongest cheap 2024 baseline and its omission would be flagged by any reviewer); P(True) self-eval with the 8 samples shown in-prompt (expected weak at 0.6B per Kadavath scaling — still report); verifier-head score alone (isolates whether the conformal COMBINER adds anything over its best feature — preregister as the internal ablation). The conformal coverage/risk guarantee (77/77 published correct, risk UCB) is reported as a separate operational claim, not conflated with the ranking-quality test.
lenses.feasibility_at_our_budget: YES — this is the one v10 claim where the evidence and the budget genuinely line up, because the fix is statistical, not architectural. The heads + conformal machinery already work at 0.6B (replicated in-house across v8/v9: coverage on target, risk UCB 0.038-0.072, directional AUGRC win on 2/2 seeds), and everything in the recipe is CPU-side except audit-row generation. The honest constraints: (a) at the observed pooled effect (z=1.04 at 576 rows), conventional alpha=0.05/90% power needs ~4,500 total audit rows — two inference-only sessions; alpha=0.05/80% needs ~3,300; the affordable single-session design (1,152 fresh/seed + ~500 reclaimed via cross-conformal ≈ 3,300 total) lands at roughly 80% power pooled, which is preregistrable and defensible. (b) The effect estimate itself is noisy (winner's-curse risk); the prereg must fix n from the conservative pooled z, not the better seed. (c) The claim upgrade is conditional on ALSO beating discrete semantic entropy from the same pool — a baseline that costs nothing here and that the current package has never faced; if the conformal combiner only beats max-logprob, the paper claim is 'beats logprob abstention', not 'state-of-the-art abstention at 0.6B'. Throughput (37 s/row measured in v9) is the only hardware number that can break the plan; it should be re-measured in the first 20 minutes of the audit session with an abort-to-800-rows fallback preregistered.
risks: Winner's curse: the power calculation is anchored on an effect estimated from the same 2 seeds that motivated it; if the true effect is at the lower end of its (wide) CI, even 4,500 rows under-deliver — preregister MDE reporting so a miss is informative, not a failed gate

Discrete semantic entropy from the existing N=8 pool may match or beat the conformal 5-feature score on short-form synthetic answers (Farquhar's wins were largest long-form; Yadkori's conformal wins over logprob also concentrated on long answers) — the headline could survive vs logprob but lose the baseline family

Effect non-stationarity: v10 retraining changes accuracy and feature distributions; delta-AUGRC scales with acc(1-acc), so if v10 audit accuracy rises toward 0.85 the absolute effect shrinks even if ranking quality is unchanged

Cross-conformal reclamation must be strictly nested (a row never scored by a fold that calibrated on it) or the coverage guarantee and test validity both silently break; this is a new code path with no in-house test coverage yet
Fixed-effect seed pooling limits the claim to 'on these two seeds'; a reviewer can demand a third seed or random-effects analysis — 2 seeds cannot estimate between-seed variance at all
Audit throughput assumption (37 s/row from v9) may not transfer to v10 mechanisms; at 60 s/row the 1,152-row/seed plan overflows the 12h session and power drops from ~80% to ~65%

lenses.lens: Do distillation/internalization recipes work through PEFT on a frozen base? (LoRA/adapter-only CoT internalization; prompt/prefix distillation with frozen decoders; rank and layer-placement requirements for teaching a frozen decoder to consume a supervised latent prefix)

papers.title: CODI: Compressing Chain-of-Thought into Continuous Space via Self-Distillation
papers.scale_tested: GPT-2 (124M) and LLaMA-3.2-1B-Instruct, base FROZEN + LoRA r=128 a=32 (bf16); GSM8k-Aug 385k rows; GPT-2: 40 epochs ~36h on 1xA100-80GB; LLaMA-1B: 10 epochs ~48h A100; effective batch 128; lr 3e-3 (GPT-2) / 8e-4 (1B)
papers.core_mechanism: LENS PREMISE CORRECTION: CODI is LoRA-only, not full FT. Joint teacher task (prompt+gold CoT+answer, CE) and student task (prompt + 6 continuous thoughts + answer, CE) SHARE the same LoRA; L1 distillation loss aligns hidden states of one designated pre-answer token (the colon before the answer) across layers, weight gamma=1 (GPT-2) / 20 (1B). Continuous thoughts are autoregressively generated hidden states passed through a small projection.
papers.measured_result: GPT-2 GSM8k: No-CoT 19.1% -> CODI 43.7% = 99% of CoT-SFT (3.1x token compression); LLaMA-1B ~90% of CoT-SFT. Ablations: remove L1 hidden-state loss 43.7->24.5; separate static teacher instead of shared-weights self-distill 43.7->27.1; remove projection 43.7->42.5. OOD (GPT-2): SVAMP 42.9 vs CoT-SFT 41.8, MultiArith 92.8 vs 90.7. Direct proof LoRA suffices for a sub-1B frozen decoder to learn to READ a latent prefix — but at 385k rows / 36-48 A100-h.

papers.title: Training Large Language Models to Reason in a Continuous Latent Space (Coconut)
papers.scale_tested: GPT-2 124M, FULL fine-tuning, GSM8k-Aug 385k rows, multi-stage curriculum (25+25 epochs in CODI's reproduction)
papers.core_mechanism: Curriculum that progressively replaces gold CoT tokens with the model's own last hidden states fed back as input embeddings; no dense distillation target.
papers.measured_result: GSM8k 34.1% — beaten by CODI's LoRA-only recipe (43.7%) despite Coconut updating all weights; shows dense hidden-state supervision matters more than unfreezing attention. Multi-stage curriculum suffers stage-forgetting.

papers.title: In-context Autoencoder for Context Compression in a Large Language Model (ICAE)
papers.scale_tested: LLaMA-7B; encoder = same LLM + LoRA r=128 on q,v projections only (~1% params, ~70M); decoder = 100% FROZEN, zero trainable reader params; pretrain AE+LM objectives on Pile, 200k updates x batch 256 on 8xA100; then 240k (context,prompt,response) instruction samples, 30k updates
papers.core_mechanism: LoRA-adapted encoder writes 128 memory-slot embeddings; frozen decoder conditions on them directly. Autoencoding (reconstruct the context from slots) is the dense supervision that forces the slots to be readable by the frozen reader.
papers.measured_result: Near-perfect reconstruction of contexts up to ~512 tokens at 4x compression; 2048 memory slots perform on par with 4096 raw tokens. Existence proof that a frozen decoder can consume latent prefixes with NO reader-side training — but only after ~50M-sequence-scale reconstruction pretraining.

papers.title: 500xCompressor: Generalized Prompt Compression for Large Language Models
papers.scale_tested: LLaMA-3-8B; encoder = frozen LLM + LoRA (~0.3% added params); decoder fully frozen; pretrained on ArXiv corpus then fine-tuned on ArxivQA; evaluated on strictly unseen QA
papers.core_mechanism: Like ICAE but injects the compressed tokens' per-layer K,V VALUES into the frozen decoder instead of input embeddings; regeneration (reconstruction) loss trains the encoder LoRA through the frozen decoder.
papers.measured_result: 62.26-72.89% of non-compressed QA capability retained at 6x-480x compression; KV-value injection measurably preserves more information than embedding injection at high compression, and not all compressed tokens are equally utilized. Design lesson for HLWM: splice the latent at KV level per layer, not as input embeddings.

papers.title: SoftCoT: Soft Chain-of-Thought for Efficient Reasoning with LLMs
papers.scale_tested: Backbone LLaMA-3.1-8B / Qwen2.5-7B / Qwen3-8B ENTIRELY frozen; assistant Qwen 0.5B/1.5B/7B or LLaMA-1B frozen; ONLY a linear projection d_assist->d_LLM trained; GSM8K 7,473 rows (matches HLWM data scale), 10 epochs, lr 1e-5, batch 8-16, single A100
papers.core_mechanism: Assistant LM reads the actual question and emits soft thought tokens = its last hidden states in one forward pass; a trained linear map projects them into the frozen backbone's embedding space as an instance-specific prefix. Latents are GROUNDED in a pretrained LM's representations, never learned from scratch.
papers.measured_result: GSM8K: LLaMA-8B 79.61->81.03, Qwen2.5 83.70->85.81 (works even with a 0.5B assistant: 85.76); AQuA 54.65->56.30. Effect size +1.3-2.1 pts. CRITICAL adversarial datapoint: their LoRA r=16 fine-tuning baseline DEGRADED GSM8K to 75.66 (catastrophic forgetting at 7.5k rows), and plain-text Assist-CoT already gets ~+1 pt, so the soft-token increment over text is ~1 pt.

papers.title: Efficient Knowledge Injection in LLMs via Prompt Distillation (Self-Distillation)
papers.scale_tested: Llama-3-8B, Qwen2.5-3B/14B instruct; student = same FROZEN model + zero-init LoRA ALL layers (default r=1024/512, ablated down to r=16); 30 self-generated questions per test question at T=1.5; 8B: 1 MI250X x 24h (~10 epochs); token-level KL to teacher distribution
papers.core_mechanism: Teacher = the model itself WITH the new document in its prompt; student = same model WITHOUT it, LoRA-adapted; loss = full-distribution KL on teacher-generated answers. Internalizes 'behavior conditioned on context you can no longer see' — the exact masked-premise structure HLWM v9 tested.
papers.measured_result: PD > SFT across all models/datasets and can beat RAG; rank ablation (NYT, Llama-8B): PD 90.9% at the LOWEST rank (16) rising to 94.7% at 1024, beating SFT at every rank; PD is 'substantially more data-efficient' than one-hot SFT with the gap widening with data. Evidence that KL-to-a-premise-visible-self-teacher works at r=16 and thousands of examples.

papers.title: Learning to Compress Prompts with Gist Tokens
papers.scale_tested: LLaMA-7B decoder and FLAN-T5-XXL, FULL instruction fine-tuning (~130k Alpaca+ instructions) with modified attention masks; NOT frozen
papers.core_mechanism: Attention-mask trick forces later tokens to attend to the prompt only through gist tokens; meta-learned compression, zero-shot to unseen instructions.
papers.measured_result: 26x prompt compression, up to 40% FLOPs reduction, minimal quality loss — but achieved with full FT; the authors explicitly defer 'retrofit a frozen LM' to future work. Follow-up (arXiv:2504.08934) reports gisting degrades on long-context/recall tasks. So gisting itself is NOT evidence for the frozen+PEFT setting; ICAE/500x are its frozen-decoder descendants.

papers.title: LoRA Learns Less and Forgets Less
papers.scale_tested: Llama-2-7B/13B; math and code; IFT ~100k pairs (MetaMathQA/Magicoder) and CPT up to 20B tokens; ranks 16/64/256; attention-only vs all-module targeting
papers.core_mechanism: Systematic LoRA-vs-full-FT comparison with SVD analysis of weight perturbations.
papers.measured_result: At r=16/64 LoRA substantially underperforms full FT on math/code; r=256 + alpha=2r + ALL modules roughly matches full FT for IFT (code r=16: 0.358 vs full-FT-matching 0.498 at r=256). Targeting all modules beats attention-only by more than a 16x rank increase. Full-FT perturbations are rank 10-100x higher than typical LoRA. Directly relevant: HLWM's r=16 all-layers is in the measured 'learns less' regime for math; the paper says raise rank before unfreezing anything.

papers.title: Prefix-Tuning+: Modernizing Prefix-Tuning through Attention Independent Prefix Data
papers.scale_tested: Modern LLMs, few-shot benchmarks (details in paper); diagnosis + architectural fix
papers.core_mechanism: Formal diagnosis of why learned prefixes fail on modern LLMs: the prefix is 'trapped' inside the attention softmax — with a long input the prefix's attention mass is diluted toward zero; with a long prefix the input is drowned. Fix: move the prefix contribution out of the attention head (additive, attention-independent).
papers.measured_result: Prefix-Tuning+ matches LoRA in few-shot settings where classical prefix-tuning collapses. Mechanistic explanation for HLWM's 42-token latent prefix being ignorable by a decoder attending over a much longer prompt — consistent with HLWM's masked-row 0.000 while a probe recovers 0.30 of the info.

papers.title: Prefix-Tuning: Optimizing Continuous Prompts for Generation
papers.scale_tested: GPT-2 medium (355M) / large, 100% FROZEN; 0.1% trainable params (per-layer KV prefix via reparameterization MLP); E2E (~42k), WebNLG (~22k), DART table-to-text
papers.core_mechanism: Task-level continuous prefix injected as per-layer key/value activations, optimized through the frozen decoder against task CE.
papers.measured_result: Comparable to full FT in full-data table-to-text and +2.9 BLEU better in low-data regimes at 355M params and 20-50k rows. Canonical proof that a frozen sub-1B decoder can consume a learned latent KV prefix at HLWM-like data scale — but the prefix is a task constant, not instance-dependent content; later work (Gu et al. 2022; 2506.13674) shows it degrades on harder/low-data reasoning settings.

lenses.recipe: Core verdict-driven design: keep the base frozen — attention does NOT need unfreezing (CODI proves LoRA-only prefix-reading at 124M/1B) — but stop asking training to invent a latent space from scratch at 7.5k rows; ground it and supervise it densely. Concretely for v10's channel: (1) GROUNDED WORKSPACE TOKENS (SoftCoT, the only recipe validated at exactly 7,473 rows / 1 GPU): the workspace's k latent tokens are the frozen base's own last-layer hidden states over the GOLD reasoning trace (or premise) at ~6-16 anchor positions, passed through ONE trainable linear d->d (lr 1e-5, 10 epochs, AdamW wd 0.01). Never free-init latents. (2) CODI SELF-DISTILLATION with shared LoRA: every batch interleaves a teacher pass (prompt + gold trace + answer, CE) and a student pass (prompt + 6 continuous thoughts + answer, CE) using the SAME LoRA; add L1 loss aligning the hidden states of one designated pre-answer token (e.g. the ':' in 'Answer:') between passes, weight gamma tuned in {1,5,20} (CODI used 20 at 1B because the distill loss magnitude shrinks); alpha=beta=1 on the two CE terms. Their ablations say this L1 term and the shared-weights teacher are the load-bearing parts (43.7->24.5 and ->27.1 without them). HLWM's synthetic gold traces make the teacher pass free.
